Imperial relations with Jarm, the Iron Confederacy, Faraden, Sarcophan, Sumaah, the Commonwealth, Asavea and Thule also shifted.

A challenging time.o: With his ritual Challenge the Iron Duke unable to be cast, Barien, the Iron Duke, announced a grand tourney for the sword Pinnacle, a year-long Victor's Challenge between Dawn and Wintermark, and an offer to patronise a contest chosen by the Archmage of Summer. Jacques Flayer of Dawn won the Pinnacle Tourney.

A circle sewn with fate.o: In spring 387YE the Grendel garrison of Mora's Rock marched out of Morajasse and, together with Oran's corsairs, routed a Children of Wrecks assault on Oran before returning to their holdfast. Commander Gallum Fiersach's forces spared the Freeborn defenders.

A dark and stormy night.o: In Autumn 387YE the Military Council shut down the Grendel espionage outpost in Spiral, and the intelligence gathered let the followers of Berechiah uncover and destroy a second Grendel spy cell hidden in the old embassy building in Cargo, Redoubt. Further Grendel 'jewels' remain in Sarvos and Madruga, with one suspected in Feroz.

A dream that can last.o: In Summer 383YE the Sand Fishers finished settling Misericorde in Holberg, which the Senate had ceded to them, and began a thriving trade in herbs and marsh goods with the League. During the Summer Solstice a covered market was commissioned for them, and the Synod passed three mandates to support them and teach them the Virtues.

A fine and private place.o: In Winter 379YE a second regio, strongly aligned to Winter, appeared at Anvil, foreshadowed by actors across the Empire unaccountably setting their plays in the Tomb. Heralds of the eternal Tharim announced that it opened onto a Winter Chamber where invited nations could offer dragonbone to the sovereign-lords of the Wasteland in return for boons.

A force to be reckoned with.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 382YE, this Wind of Fortune surveyed the Empire's relations with the great powers and its smaller neighbours, centred on the planned Imperial Slavery Summit. The summit proved a resounding success and committed the Empire to trade sanctions against slaving nations.

A fork in the path.o: Returning from their exploration of Tsirku, the Mystics of Ishal reorganised the help they give Wintermark and the Raven Seer. They ended the Parliament of Owls, offered the Raven's Dream in exchange for true liao, set out new rules for crowning a Champion of Wintermark, and brought offers of aid against threats from the Gullet.

A friend like you.o: In Autumn 388YE a host of eternals sought to influence the Empire, offering great works, a Dawnish college of magic and an oath against the Cold Sun, while laying down challenges and threatening curses in several territories.

A fundamental struggle (Trade Winds).o: In Spring 380YE Imperial fleet captains brought back news of shifting foreign relations: the Sumaah remained at war with the Empire, Asavea and the Eastern Jarmish princes were friendly, and the Commonwealth imposed strict searches, tariffs and restrictions on Imperial ships.

A glorious victory.o: Dawn and its allies shattered the Druj armies and conquered the Barrens, at the cost of the Hounds of Glory, who were broken storming the Spires of Dusk. The Senate granted Dawn dominion over the territory, setting off nationwide celebration and a set of choices about how to secure the victory.

A greater darkness.o: In Autumn 388YE Navarr and Imperial Orc warbands, aided by heralds of Irra Harah and the Karass sept, raided the Mallum to free the Great Forest Orcs enslaved in the Druj weirwood groves. Those freed from the Grove of Woe reached the Empire, but about four hundred freed from the Sacred Grove were left trapped in the Forest of Ulnak.

A habit I can't break.o: An Autumn 388YE roundup of strange events: the Imperial Menagerie's rakshasa died of old age and three parties sought its body, the hakima sent the City of Wonders' arcane projection to Anvil, Navarr's dream-song faded, Rivers of Life and Rivers Run Red changed their relationship, and coral husks stirred in Bregasland and Kallavesa.

A health to the company.o: In Winter 383YE the Holberg University College of Engineering sought Senate permission to expand and challenged the League to begin an impressive commission in each of its four cities, offering a Chair of the Wolf in return. The page also set out opportunities in Holmauer Park, at Georgie's House and at Mellfort; the Senate approved the expansion of Georgie's House.

A heap of broken images.o: In Winter 379YE the displaced Hierro clan of Lasambrian orcs, camped in Segura and taught the Way by Imperial missionaries, grew bolder, formally asked to join the Empire as a new nation with a homeland, and strained relations with their Freeborn neighbours. The Synod answered with judgements urging tolerance and orthodox instruction.

A hero's welcome.o: Imperial fleets returning from the raid on the Grendel at Dubhtraig were welcomed as heroes, bringing treasure and nearly two thousand freed slaves, most of them orcs of the Broken Shore with nowhere to go. At the Winter Solstice the Synod's General Assembly upheld a mandate settling the freed orcs in Skarsind and another bringing them the Way.

A horn blast of victory.o: In Summer 388YE Emperor Vesna, newly crowned Queen of Dawn after the manticore's defeat, addressed the Empire and called the Dawnish to destroy the Druj. Her words filled Dawn's armies with eagerness for glorious charges against the orcs.

A horn resounding.o: Kirsa Wordsmith, a scop of Hahnmark, sounded the century-old Horn of Hope at Rundhal during the Summer Solstice, shattering it, and months later a wave of Summer magic caused many Imperial children to age suddenly by one to three years. The phenomenon drew the interest of the Academy, a Highborn chapter and numerous eternals.

A job worth doing.o: After the Autumn Equinox 379YE, a band of scaled, lizard-like Summer creatures calling themselves koboldi arrived at the Castle of Thorns in Astolat and, within two days, repaired all the damage left by a recent Winter curse before vanishing. They claimed to serve King Adamant, a Summer eternal previously unknown in the Empire, and had been summoned by the Urizeni Spire of the Auric Horizon.

A knock at the door.o: In Spring 388YE the independent city-state of Beoraidh, now under Sarcophan Delves protection, named Rubhart Kaltrin as its ambassador to the Empire and renewed offers of trade, temple-building and diplomacy. Separately, a coalition of reavers proposed raiding the Brine Turtles sept in Mareave, seeking a mandate from the Imperial Orc assembly.

A lasting commitment.o: In Summer 388YE the Ambition Assembly declared completing the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion within a single year to be its highest calling, while the Highborn Assembly began deciding how the vast edifice should be laid out and who should occupy it.

A long December.o: Following the Winter Solstice, the Department of Historical Research was left badly stretched after staff were retrained as prognosticators and assigned to vallorn research, while the Whisper Gallery renewed its murderous campaign against Imperial scholars. The Imperial Archivist set out changes to the Department and a plan to fight back.

A long good-bye.o: In the autumn of 379YE, priests of vigilance led a League-wide campaign against the vyig in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar that broke the criminal conspiracy, although the disruption cut business incomes in those cities for the season.

A lost king.o: The Imperial Orcs completed two of the three great follies promised to the orc septs from Ossium: the Black Forge for the Ethengraw and the Bone Temple ossuary for the Illarawm. The septs resolved to join the Imperial Orcs together at the Autumn Equinox, once the Yerende garden is finished.

A mountain of vipers.o: Following a Summer Solstice Synod mandate urging trade with Axos, a series of time-limited Axou trade and diplomatic opportunities opened to the Empire in Autumn 383YE. They included a new port at Issyk, a liao market, white granite for dragonbone and a student exchange with Maykop.

A murder of one.o: In Spring 385YE, Hallow of the Green World pried open Spring regio across the Empire. Boggarts spilled out, Grimmelkint swarms threatened every Imperial forest, Arhallogen urged the Navarr to slaughter the Jotun, and Siakha offered a short truce through a Grendel high priestess.

A peerless sacrifice.o: Highguard was forced to choose between keeping its power of peerless kinship towards other nations and its armies' power of crusade. The Highborn Assembly enacted a mandate retaining peerless kinship, and the Benefactors' Council chose to keep supporting the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

A pillow of winds.o: In Spring 387YE the Civil Service reported on relations with Faraden. The Court of the Five Winds welcomed the Imperial invasion of Reinos but could not give military aid because of its treaty with the Jotun, and the report set out trade, magical and religious opportunities.

A pinch of salt.o: The smiths freed from the Woldstone in Summer 386YE, having recovered with the monks of Oakwood, offered the Marches the chance to commission a Stone Smith's Workshop at either the Woldstone in Upwold or the Maiden Stone in Mitwold, creating the title of Stone Smith.

A place on a map.o: In Spring 384YE, the civil servant Mladen Escovitch delivered the Senate-requested appraisal of how each Urizen territory might be fortified, including Druj-held Zenith and Grendel-held Spiral. He named fortification opportunities, and their costs, for each.

A pleasing and deceptive face.o: Following the Summer Solstice, six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages for the Autumn Equinox 383YE: five agreed to meetings of some kind, Yaw'nagrah declined, and a little-known Spring eternal calling itself "Lord Rain" unexpectedly requested a formal parley.

A question of loyalty.o: In Autumn 385YE, Urizen spires in Spiral rebelled against the Empire and seized Ankra and Cinion, after the Loyalty Assembly's Eyes of Loyalty amplified Hector's Urizen Assembly mandate. Naomi of Virtue's Rest set out the rebel factions' demands and possible remedies.

A question of provenance.o: Spring magic tied to the eternal Llofir left strange, nourishing but unsettling mushrooms and plants across Reikos, and the Synod was asked to guide the Highborn on whether to shun or use them. The Highborn Assembly backed an exclusionist message, strengthening the congregations of Reikos at the cost of its production.

A season of mushrooms.o: In Summer 380YE a surge of Spring magic, believed by magisters to be directed by the eternal Llofir and heightened by the Hallow of the Green World, swept Reikos, devouring the dead, the ruined and the Druj taint and leaving a wild, natural landscape in its place.

A spiritual prism.o: In Spring 381YE the Synod's rejection of Yael's Doctrine of the Beyond split the Empire along lines of faith: nations whose assemblies decisively rejected her could no longer fight effectively alongside those that had not, Highborn armies began to falter, and new opportunities opened for Yael's supporters.

A star is born.o: An Imperial expedition of fifteen military units and seventy-one fleets sailed to the Sea of Steel to aid the former slaves of Rachensgrab. It found them prospering in the Commonwealth, and instead discovered the guarded island kingdom of the Viyerda, whose bay yields ilium from falling stars.

A stone for a stone.o: Commissioned by the Imperial Senate, Naomi of Virtue's Rest appraised what might make peace more appealing to the Jotun. She concluded that a lasting peace was near impossible, but set out steps that could make a temporary ceasefire achievable, and reported two Lasambrian peace offers.

A strange land.o: After the Senate assigned newly conquered Ossium to Varushka, a series of opportunities arose for the territory: fortifying and arming the town of Ketsov, resettling the Sand Fishers, upgrading the Crawling Depths mines and preaching the Way to its people. The Senate ceded Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, and the Pride assembly passed a mandate to preach in Ossium.

A tale told.o: In Autumn 385YE seven Imperial armies, backed by elite warbands and Summer, Winter, Autumn and Shadowed Fire allies, invaded the Jotun territory of Tromsa from Sermersuaq. They conquered Icewood, Skyfall Waste and Rikskog, killed Jarl Olgaf, and then stalled before the adamant-reinforced fortress of Oksenesfestsal in Tromsdalen.

A thousand steps.o: Having committed to war against the vallorn, the Navarr faced the urgent problem of paying for the new army being raised in Hercynia, and this wind set out several ways to fund it and win allies. It also revealed ghostly hauntings at the Seren temple site and announced a conjunction there.

A thousand years of longing.o: The expanded Great Library of Hacynian completed its research into the vallorn years ahead of schedule, gathering everything known about its creation and concluding that linking every remaining vallorn heart to the trods would rouse it fully and make it vulnerable to final defeat.

A throne of blood.o: With spring easing the harsh winter, Dogri Thulebane, still occupying Crow's Ridge in northern Skarsind, sent word that he would meet Imperial representatives at Crowskeep on strict terms, as die-hard Winterfolk continued to rally to his banner.

A tide in the affairs.o: In Summer 385YE the League's Wolves of War crossed through the Twilight Gate and secured all of Spiral in a single season under Salt Lord Kaliact's treaty with the Senate, making it a League territory of the Empire. They met little organised resistance but lost soldiers to the Black Plateau's miasma.

A time of plenty.o: After Gilah of the Chantry consecrated Zemress' ship, the Kraken's Bane, with true liao at Calvos Sound, the architect Gabriela i Matez i Riqueza i Zemress proposed a seminary built on a wharf beside it. The Senate commissioned the seminary, and Sumaash support was secured provided work began on time.

A victory for diplomacy.o: In Autumn 386YE the Iron Confederacy accepted the Senate's Free Trade and narcotics-ban treaty and stayed out of the Freedom Accord. After three Suranni delegations visited Anvil, the Iron Dukes lifted their sanctions on Imperial merchants trading at Robec.

A walk in shadow.o: In Autumn 385YE the Citadel Guard, Valiant Pegasus, Gryphon's Pride and Iron Helms crossed the Nameless River from Saltmarsh into the Druj heartland of the Salt Flats of Sanath. Stiff Druj resistance in the Sydathian Fens drove them back to their first fortified camp, but the Imperial armies held on.

A wandering fire.o: In Autumn 384YE an Imperial and Thule alliance stormed the Jotun citadels of Olgafsdottirshal in Tanikipari and the Fortress of Kalant in Stark, driving the Jotun entirely out of Sermersuaq. Afterwards the Thule warned of a Jotun plot to unleash Hayaak's heralds on their warlocks, and several further opportunities arose in the territory.

A wild night and a new road.o: The Civil Service's Winter 387YE report on relations with the Sarcophan Delves covered continued Imperial access to the Jakhalsmarkt and a Sarcophan offer of mercenaries against the Children of Wrecks. It also covered the five-year anniversary party at the Alivetti estates in Sarvos, proposals to police that enclave, herbal trade with the Apothecaries' Guild and the Highborn monument trade.

A wisdom of questions.o: After the Urizen Assembly called on sword scholars to stop venerating Sulemaine, several opportunities followed. A Urizen mandate could split the sword scholar movement, Highborn priests proposed a law requiring Synod approval to consecrate tombs, and Dawn's Assembly could embrace sword scholar teaching at Laroc.

A wizard did it.o: A roundup of strange magical happenings in Summer 388YE: the astronomantic chaos continued, Mareave briefly bloomed under a wayward Rivers of Life, the Painted Caves enchantment became permanent, and odd dreams, songs and superstitions spread across the Empire.

A yellow star hung.o: In the Autumn of 384YE, magical fortifications, veils and restored trods followed the Summer Solstice. Rejuvenating rains fell on Zenith while savage storms struck the Barrens, and assorted curses, dreams, conjunctions and new Urizen lore emerged across the Empire.

About today.o: In Winter 386YE the Civil Service reported on relations with Otkodov, with the peace treaty due to expire at the Summer Solstice 387YE. The report also covered a planned cultural exchange, a Thule consortium repaying its bonds, and two conjunctions involving troubled Thule bands.

Abrogate Moonwater Hall.o: In Summer 384YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Reikos and seconded by Semmerholm, to abrogate Moonwater Hall, the Faraden trade hub in Upwold. The hall was largely demolished and the Faraden were told to stop gathering there.

Abrogate motion to construct the Signori.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Zenith, to abrogate its earlier decision that same summit to construct the Signori d'Argento Vineyards sinecure in Sarvos.

Accept Barrens peace treaty.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate defeated a motion to accept a treaty negotiated by a delegation of Barrens orcs and humans, which would have set terms for Imperial troops moving through the Barrens.

Accept Grendel proposal.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate formally accepted a proposal from the Grendel Salt Lord of Dubhtraig: the Grendel would withdraw one of their armies from Spiral if the Empire did not raid Dubhtraig for a year.

Accept Jotun ceasefire.o: In Summer 377YE the Senate accepted the Jotun offer of a two-year ceasefire, passing the motion by 27 votes to 0, so that neither the Jotun nor the Empire would make war on the other.

Accept Orcs of the Great Forest treaty.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion ratifying a peace treaty with the Orcs of the Great Forest, recognising them as a sovereign foreign nation. The orcs, formerly of the Barrens, became officially foreigners and were granted residence in the Lower Tarn Valley of Therunin.

Accept Sarcophan Delves treaty.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed a motion ratifying a trade treaty with the Sarcophan Bedelaar-Huisbaas Vandersaar, under which the Empire could buy 24 wains of white granite each season. A cargo dock and ministerial offices were to be built in Redoubt to receive it.

Accept Thule peace treaty.o: In Summer 379YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Morrow, to accept a peace treaty negotiated by a Thule delegation. The recorded outcome set out a three-year cessation of hostilities between the Thule and the Empire.

Accomplices.o: Agramant's heralds in Therunin derided the Empire for sending only the Golden Axe and two military units to retake Lower Tarn Valley. The Bloody Ally offered heart's blood to any unit supporting an Imperial attack there, while the outlaw Dochas Weeping Glade invited Imperial representatives to a Sentinel Gate meeting to plan the territory's liberation.

According to principle.o: The Civil Service's Winter 386YE summary of relations with the Commonwealth reported that a party of Commonwealth scholars under Professor Immanuel Gelberg had arrived in Sarvos to offer appraisals in return for donations to their war against Jarm. It also covered sweeping changes to trade at Leerdam and Volkavaar.

Across the Abyss.o: After Imperial forces drove a Druj army out of Holberg in Winter 383YE, the Sand Fishers embraced the Virtues, especially Prosperity, with new fervour and began petitioning the Empire for education, lore and development. They also asked what they could give the Empire in return.

Across the seven seas.o: Through the past season, every fleet belonging to Navarr and Varushkan captains carried a potent Summer enchantment, so those who went privateering or traded with foreign ports met strange adventures at sea and came home with extra booty. The magic came from scrolls delivered at the Winter Solstice by heralds of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Ocean.

Address boggart infestation in Morrow.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Necropolis, to trap the boggarts infesting Morrow and stop them damaging its mana sites.

After the gold rush.o: Ahead of the Summer Solstice 383YE, a series of opportunities arose at Anvil: a Wintermark thane's storytelling contest, two auctions by heralds of Autumn, a mysterious presence in a Navarr night regio, a Brass Coast fleet offered for sale, and a Holberg military unit seeking a new patron.

Against the Jotun.o: In Winter 385YE the Imperial armies withdrew from Tromsa after defeating the new Jarl and taking Mathilda Fisher, and a vast Jotun force swiftly reclaimed the territory. Most of the remaining armies then invaded the Iron Stand in Skallahn and fought to a bloody stalemate below Oversgaard, while the Lasambrian Jotun invaded Kahraman again.

All I ask of you.o: An Imperial Orc delegation under Skywise Rykana, sent to learn about the Great Forest Orc ancestors, found that the Druj were threatening to impale thousands of enslaved Great Forest Orcs unless Chief Vallack collaborated. This opened an opportunity for the Navarr and Imperial Orcs to organise a rescue raid into Druj lands.

All I can do.o: The General Assembly's backing for a Basilica of the Way in the independent city-state of Beoraidh brought forward several offers to help fund and build it, alongside a chance for the Senate to extend the Regario Dossier's spies into the city. After the Autumn Equinox 388YE, Bloodcrow Rasp and Herminius of the House of the Wanderer provided the twenty Thrones needed to buy the land.

All along the watchtower.o: In Summer 381YE the people of the Mournwold turned bitterly against the Empire after Imperial Spring curses killed a sixth of the population and the Iron Helms waged a campaign of terror against the Jotun. The civil service set out several partial remedies, and the Marcher assembly answered by mandating that no Marcher army would ever give ground.

All at sea.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 383YE, this Wind of Fortune surveyed the Empire's relations with foreign powers. Relations with Asavea and Jarm worsened, ties with the Sarcophan Delves, Commonwealth and Axos grew warmer, smuggling across the Brass Coast's western border was confirmed, and the Thule freed their last Imperial slaves.

All in red.o: In Summer 384YE, Faraden anger at the Senate's abrogation of Moonwater Hall boiled over: Modnos arsonists burned the Blood Red River Museum in Tassato and Spider's Vantage Spire in Redoubt, and a bloodless coup soon put the Ganbatar family in charge of Faraden.

All laudable qualities.o: In Summer 388YE the civil service published the timetable for the Proscription Symposium led by Wulfric of the Marches, alongside magistrates' guidance on religious crimes and details of invited guests: the Constitutional Court, the Mournwold orcs and two Lucidian groups.

All lift together.o: The Wintermark National Assembly's call for more healing herbs to support Asny of Storm Spire and the nation's warriors stirred debate among the grimnir, who put forward several ways to secure herbs. The Senate went on to commission the Healing House of Wittal Grove at the Winter Solstice, though problems with the motion left the Constitutional Court to resolve them.

All my magic friends.o: A Winter 385YE Wind of Fortune gathered many smaller magical happenings across the Empire, from a fading Winter curse over Casinea and a risen dead village in Miekarova to offers, challenges and complaints from eternals including Arhallogen, the Azoth, Kaela, Barien, Jaheris and Tharim.

All the news from Twin Town.o: In Autumn 383YE the twin cities of Tassato, enjoying relative peace while other League cities suffered, put forward several proposals: an Imperial Consulate in Regario, two trade projects with Navarr prompted by a statement inviting Seren to join the League, and sanctuary for the Whittle folk. A rumoured incident also struck the Arratan Gamble quarries in Enterio.

All the night-tide.o: Sarcophan relations with the Empire in Autumn 387YE centred on the Pax Sarcophan against piracy, a planned treaty with Beoraidh, and an offer to invest in a new Celesti Lighthouse. The season also brought new trading opportunities, proposals for the Apothecaries' Guild, and fallout from the trade in Highborn art.

All the way.o: In Spring 384YE the Lasambrian Jotun abandoned Segura after recovering ancestral relics from the Caida, letting Imperial armies liberate Anduz, then promptly invaded Kahraman through western Gambit alongside the Yegarra of the Mournwold.

All the way to Anvil.o: Ahead of the Autumn Equinox 386YE, word spread of a number of visitors heading to Anvil, each with their own business: grievances, experiments, magical opportunities, offers from the realms and a plan to reclaim the ruined Vale of Bulgakov.

All the wind.o: In Winter 386YE the Faraden ambassador rebuffed Imperial approaches over the Asavean attack on Meade, while Celestial Arch emissaries toured Faraden wizard families and found Asavean influence spreading. The Court of Five Winds also proposed a Faraden trading enclave in Holberg and a parador at the Azure Chorus.

All those moments.o: In Winter 385YE a dark wind swept the Barrens after the Druj were driven out: the Montanians were slaughtered by the Northern Eagle, the Black Wind's leaders were executed by the Iron Helms, and the Karass all but wiped out the Vendarri. The surviving orc factions were left in shock, the Druj spread the news to deepen fear of the Empire, and the Synod's authority suffered.

All too well.o: A year after the Ossium septs settled in Skarsind, the Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende still stood apart from the Imperial Orcs. A fiery preacher, Stonecliff Brakkalo, urged the nation to withdraw from the Empire's wars, while each sept made its own overture.

All work together.o: In Winter 381YE the Synod weighed rival mandates arising from Nina of Cantiarch's Hold's statement of principle urging the Empire to follow the Way more closely. Severin Teyhard von Holberg's mandate calling for unity around the seven Virtues passed by the largest margin.

Allocate Crawling Depths.o: In Autumn 382YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Tassato and seconded by Holberg, making the mithril mine known as the Crawling Depths in Ossium an Imperial Bourse seat.

Allocate Great Forest.o: A Senate motion to allocate the Great Forest at Reikos bourse seat as a national bourse position for Highguard failed in Spring 380YE. A subsequent motion allocating it as an Imperial position passed instead.

Allocate Great Forest II.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 380YE allocating the Great Forest bourse seat in Reikos as an Imperial position, following an earlier failed attempt to make it a national seat.

Allocate Great Pits of Ennerlund.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 379YE to allocate the Great Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg as an Imperial bourse position, while the mithril mine was still being repaired after its destruction by the Druj.

Allocate Legacy.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed a motion allocating the Legacy, a bourse seat in Ossuary in Spiral, as a national position.

Allocate The Brilliant Shore.o: In Autumn 377YE the Senate voted 21 to 4 to make the Brilliant Shore, a White Granite source in Skarsind, a National Bourse position for Wintermark, but the Imperial Synod vetoed the motion. The question was raised again automatically at the Winter Solstice 377YE, passed, and the Brilliant Shore became a National Bourse position.

Allocate the Great Mine of Briante.o: In Autumn 380YE the Senate passed a motion to allocate the Great Mine of Briante, a bourse seat in Kahraman, as an Imperial Bourse position.

Allocate the Pride of Ikka's Tears.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Madruga and seconded by Bastion, allocating the new mithril mine in Sermersuaq as a Wintermark national Bourse position named the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Allocate the Singing Caves.o: The Senate considered a motion, proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Hahnmark, to allocate the recently liberated Singing Caves in the Mournwold as a national position, with the Marches and the League put forward as candidates.

Allocate the Singing Caves II.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Upwold and seconded by Mitwold, allocating the Singing Caves in Mournwold, which the Empire had recovered, as an Imperial bourse position.

Allocate the Singing Caves III.o: In Autumn 381YE Holberg proposed, with Bregasland seconding, a Senate motion to allocate the Bourse seat for the Singing Caves in Mournwold, recently recovered by the Empire. The motion was withdrawn and the seat was left unallocated.

Allocate the Singing Caves Spring 382YE.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Astolat, to allocate the Singing Caves mithril mine in the Mournwold as a national Bourse position.

Allocate the Vigilant Swan.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion to assign the newly liberated Vigilant Swan bourse seat in Reikos as a national position for the Imperial Orcs, but the General Assembly of the Synod vetoed it.

Alongside the Earthquake Drummers.o: In Spring 388YE Imperial warbands fighting as mercenaries alongside the Thule army the Earthquake Drummers helped Otkodov's forces conquer Oerwealt in the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak and push three-quarters of the way through the Bonewall. The Great Pit remained untaken.

Alter the works of Almodin Oktístis.o: The Senate passed a motion in Spring 383YE to remove the heretical elements from several Imperial works built by the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis, at a cost of 92 thrones and 4 crowns.

Ambassadors of death.o: In Summer 388YE five eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages of the Imperial archmages, while no Night parley took place because Archmage Bella Vicente d'Apulian resigned amid treason rumours without sending one. Kaela, Prospero, Meraud, Roshanwe and Irra Harah each set out terms, offers or grievances.

Amend Memorial Gardens of Treji.o: The Senate passed a motion in Summer 382YE transferring the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji from a Navarr national title to an Imperial Orc national title, as a gesture of friendship after the two peoples jointly liberated Hercynia.

Amend Spires of Dusk.o: In Spring 386YE the Senate passed a motion to remodel the Spires of Dusk, a fortification in the Barrens, stripping away its Druj elements and making it a monument to the sacrifice of the Hounds of Glory.

Amend Virtue's Respite.o: In Spring 388YE the Senate passed a motion to amend Virtue's Respite in Hanuri, Temeschwar, into the "Bloody Massive Pride of Temeschwar", an opportunity arising from The concisest tenant Wind of Fortune. Once complete, its title was renamed the Bloody Custodian of Pride.

Amend conditions of Brock's Buffet.o: In Spring 378YE the Senate rejected a motion to let the Navarr compete in Brock's Buffet, the annual contest of arms between Dawnish and Marcher yeomen that decides custodianship of Brock's Toll in Miaren.

Amend motion to construct runeforge in R.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate amended its earlier motion to build a runeforge in Redoubt so that the construction would use the services of the Asavean architect.

Amend motion to fortify Karsk.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed an amendment to its earlier motion to build a fortification in Lestasny, Karsk, so that the work would use the Asavean architect.

Amend powers of Dredgemaster of Feverwat.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate passed a motion improving the Feverwater Lake sinecure and granting the Dredgemaster of Feverwater the power to commission one piece of historical research each season.

Amend the use of the Gardens of High Cha.o: The Senate passed a motion, proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Necropolis, to redirect the herbs produced by the Gardens of High Chalcis to the orcs of the Great Forest living in Therunin.

Amend the use of the Imperial breadbaske.o: In Summer 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Skarsind, repurposing the Imperial Breadbasket to supply free food to the people of the Mournwold who were not in an army.
A Senate motion proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Skarsind sought to permanently change the Imperial Breadbasket to include the Mournwold. The motion failed.

An affirming flame.o: Urizen took stock of the foreign help it had received against the Druj and Grendel, and was offered ways to thank the League generals and the Highborn armies. Furia Severia's Three Watchers, colossal statues of Highborn soldiers, were created by ritual and consecrated with true liao.

An angry blade.o: Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra, instructed by the Senate to find ways for Imperial fleet captains to disrupt Grendel naval and logistical operations in the Bay of Catazar, concluded that fleets cannot directly oppose a Grendel navy without an Imperial navy to support. She offered four alternative proposals instead.

An apple that falls.o: In Autumn 381YE the Mournwold stood on the brink of sedition despite the Jotun being nearly driven out, angry over the Empire's ritual slaughter and the new Imperial Warmage's address. The wind set out the Mourn's grievances and a range of possible Imperial responses.

An arrow nocked and in flight.o: In Spring 388YE Commander Gallum Fiersach of the Protectorate of Morajasse, recognised by the Senate as foreign and distinct from the Grendel, asked to deal with the Empire through the Imperial Consul. He offered to concede the Spice Gardens of Feroz in return for Freeborn-grown food for his garrison at Mora's Rock.

An eagle in song.o: After the Assembly of Pride called for a memorial to the Dawnish troubadour and exemplar Ozren de Orzel, the civil service offered three sites for an inspirational academy. The General Assembly chose Belletain in Sandling, Weirwater, though the academy had not yet been commissioned.

An ideal for living.o: Following an Urizen National Assembly judgement, Urizen's rival sword scholar sects gathered at the ruined Temple of the Winds in Peregro, Morrow, and agreed to unite under the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden and return to the Imperial fold. They offered the chance to rebuild the temple, which would come with mandates able to blunt religious influence over Urizen and potentially the whole Empire.

An iron feast.o: Barien's heralds announced two new challenges for the Autumn 387YE summit: the Challenge of the Eternal Banquet, a cooking contest built around a secret ingredient, and the Challenge of the Noble Hunt, in which unarmed challengers seek hidden trophies while being hunted by Jaheris' heralds.

An old sodality.o: The Constitutional Court confirmed that the Sun Chamber, an ancient sodality founded under Empress Richilde to help young citizens gain high office, still legally exists. It was revived at Anvil with civil service support, and the eternal Roshanwe offered its members gifts and an audience with a herald.

An unexpected alignment.o: In Winter 383YE a Thule delegation led by the general Hoosfa Mek arrived at Sealtoq under a flag of truce, offering up to three Thule armies to support an Imperial reconquest of Sermersuaq from the Jotun in exchange for Imperial regions and captured orc thralls. The Senate went on to ratify a treaty with the Thule securing their aid in Sermersuaq.

Anarchy in Miekarova.o: In Winter 378YE an organised anarchy cult spread malign auras and sabotaged supply lines for military units based in Miekarova, threatening their effectiveness while briefly boosting local trade. The Vigilance Assembly responded by naming Vitomir Vardov to raise virtuous auras across the territory.

Another verse.o: In Summer 386YE, four Imperial armies backed by the Knights of Glory and Imperial captains drove the Lasambrian Jotun and two further Jotun armies out of Kahraman, liberating the territory at a cost of nearly three and a half thousand Imperial soldiers.

Any dream will do.o: After the League Assembly declared it their highest calling to bring sapient beings of every kind into the Empire, the Way of Virtue and the League, the League gained a year-long opportunity to court new partners for the Great Game.

Any port in a storm.o: In Autumn 387YE Naomi of Virtue's Rest completed a Senate-ordered appraisal of building a great port, the Imperatrix Docks, in Utterlund on Holberg's coast, with offers of help from the Sarcophan Lijkkever family and the Sand Fisher orcs. The Senate could now commission it.

Anyone but you.o: In spring 385YE the Empire's efforts to root out Agramant's cults in reclaimed Sermersuaq bore fruit: the Silent Bell exposed the ringleaders, Wintermark's priests and Stormcrows won clemency for remorseful cultists, and the Shuttered Lantern recovered the Howler's boons. Three notorious cult leaders escaped, and new threats were uncovered.

Apparently with no surprise.o: Ahead of the 387YE Winter Solstice, word arrived of visitors travelling to Anvil to meet citizens. They included a Sarcophan funeral procession, rival merchants seeking Hahnmark farmers, alders from Jotun-assailed Mitwold, Urizen seers, Highborn herbalists, envoys of the Charnel Lord and a Freeborn sect answering an inquisition. A Highborn mendicant was also trapped in caves beneath Casfall.

Apples from a tree.o: In Winter 383YE the civil service set out new and lingering chances to build national markets that divert Bourse resources from the public auction: the Kauppahall in Valashal, expanded docks at Korotny, the Blackfield Market and the Parador of Dust. Abbess Jenny Stock also proposed that the Cardinal of Prosperity use Synod mandates to seek commercial opportunities in named territories.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 382.o: The Senate passed a motion to appoint an Ambassador to Otkodov in Spring 382YE, and Yvengi Katzev was elected to the post.

Appoint Ambassador to Otkodov Spring 383.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion to elect an Ambassador to Otkodov, and the incumbent, Yevgeni Katzev, was reappointed to the post.

Appoint Commonwealth ambassador.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate made the first appointment to the new post of Ambassador to the Commonwealth, choosing Beatrix Amalia Novarian Zu Holberg.

Appoint Dean of the Academy Summer 382YE.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion to appoint a new Dean of the Academy, and Morana was elected to the post.

Appoint Dean of the Liberated.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by Miaren and seconded by Feroz, to appoint a Dean of the Liberated, the ceremonial title attached to the College of the Liberated in Sarvos. Venturo de Sarvos was appointed to the position.

Appoint Feverwater Dredgemaster.o: In Spring 378YE the Navarr senators unanimously appointed Corey Brackensong as Dredgemaster of Lake Feverwater, a procedural appointment to the position created by an earlier motion permitting the dredging of Feverwater.

Appoint Sumaah ambassador.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate raised a motion, proposed by Miaren and seconded by Zenith, to appoint an Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic. When the election was held at the Winter Solstice no candidate won the Senate's backing, so the post stayed vacant.

Appoint Throne IV.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate attempted to elect a new Throne, but no single candidate received enough votes and no one was appointed.

Appoint Throne V.o: In Spring 380YE the Senate held an election for the Throne, proposed by Volodmartz and seconded by Therunin, and Lisabetta von Holberg was elected Empress.

Appoint Thule Ambassador.o: In Spring 381YE the Senate passed an administrative motion creating the post of Imperial ambassador to the Thule, and Juha, the Cave Spider was appointed to it.

Appraisal of Feni dispersion.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate considered a motion, proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Hahnmark, to have the civil service appraise the cost of using the militia or private citizens to disperse or arrest the northern Woods-that-Fell Feni in Hercynia. The motion failed.

Appraisal of integration of Mournwold Or.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion commissioning a civil service appraisal into integrating the orc thralls of the Mournwold into the Marcher nation, with a report due before the Summer Solstice.

Appraise Sign of Tamar.o: In Autumn 383YE the Senate passed a motion to appraise how the Sign of Tamar in Tamarbode, Reikos, might be saved from being reclaimed by the forest, and how the Empire might use it once preserved.

Archive:376YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.o: This was the roll of Imperial titles held at the Winter Solstice of 376YE, listing the senators, generals, Synod cardinals and gatekeepers, Conclave archmagi and grandmasters, and holders of Bourse positions.

Archive:377YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.o: Following the 377YE Autumn Equinox, this archive listed the holders of Imperial titles across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave, Bourse and mercantile offices. It also recorded the vacant Warmage title, the vetoed Brilliant Shore allocation and Bourse seats lost to the Druj.

Archive:377YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.o: This archived record listed who held the Empire's titles at the Spring Equinox 377YE, including senators, generals, Synod cardinals and gatekeepers, archmagi, grandmasters and Bourse seat holders.

Archive:377YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: This was the record of who held the Empire's Senate seats, Military Council posts, Synod and Conclave offices and Bourse positions after the Summer Solstice 377YE.

Archive:377YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.o: This is the record of who held the Empire's Imperial titles after the Winter Solstice of 377YE. It covers the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:378YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.o: This archive recorded who held the Empire's Imperial titles after the 378YE Autumn Equinox, covering the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:378YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.o: This page recorded who held the Empire's principal titles at the Spring Equinox 378YE, covering the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse. It also noted several changes of general and one vacant Senate seat.

Archive:378YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: A record of who held the Empire's titles at the Summer Solstice of 378YE, covering the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:378YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.o: This archive page recorded who held the Empire's Imperial titles as of the Winter Solstice 378YE, across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:379YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.o: This archive recorded who held the Empire's titles at the Autumn Equinox of 379YE across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse, from senators and generals to archmagi, cardinals and Bourse seat holders.

Archive:379YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.o: This was the roster of Imperial title-holders at the Spring Equinox of 379YE, listing the senators, generals, Synod and Conclave officers, Bourse seat holders and other appointed positions across the Empire.

Archive:379YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: This was the record of who held the Empire's titles after the Summer Solstice of 379YE, covering the Senate, the Military Council, the Synod, the Conclave, the Bourse and assorted sinecures. It also noted that the Quartermaster General, Irontide Rad, died during the Solstice.

Archive:379YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.o: This archive recorded who held the Empire's titles at the 379YE Winter Solstice, covering the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:380YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.o: The roster of Imperial title holders at the Autumn Equinox 380YE, with Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League on the Throne, recorded every senator, general, Synod post, Conclave officer and Bourse seat.

Archive:380YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.o: This archive recorded who held the Empire's principal titles at the Spring Equinox 380YE, when Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League was Empress, across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:380YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: The register of Imperial title-holders at the Summer Solstice 380YE recorded Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg on the Throne, with the senators, generals, Synod, Conclave and Bourse office-holders of that moment.

Archive:380YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.o: This archive recorded who held the Empire's titles after the Winter Solstice 380YE, with Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg on the Throne. It covered the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:381YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.o: This archive recorded who held the Empire's titles at the Autumn Equinox 381YE, with Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League on the Throne.

Archive:381YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.o: This was the record of who held the Empire's titles at the 381YE Spring Equinox, covering the Throne, Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse. Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League sat on the Throne as Empress.

Archive:381YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: At the Summer Solstice of 381YE, the Empire's officeholders were recorded across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse, with Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League on the Throne.

Archive:381YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.o: At the 381YE Winter Solstice the Empire recorded who held its titles under Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League: senators, generals, Synod and Conclave offices, Bourse seats and lesser posts. Several posts stood vacant, including the senatorship of Temeschwar and the generalship of Varushka's Golden Axe.

Archive:382YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.o: This is the record of who held the Empire's titles at the Spring Equinox 382YE, with Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League on the Throne. It lists the holders of positions in the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse.

Archive:382YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.o: The record of Imperial titles at the Summer Solstice 382YE listed the holders of offices across the Senate, Military Council, Synod, Conclave and Bourse, with Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League on the Throne.

Archive:Paid Work Autumn Equinox 384YE.o: This archive page recorded the citizens who took paid work at the Autumn Equinox 384YE, listing each by name and nation across three separate tables.

Archive:Roll of Honour Spring Equinox 38.o: The Roll of Honour for the Spring Equinox 388YE recorded the Imperial citizens who lent their support to armies, fleets and spy networks that season. It is notable for a large Wintermark effort behind a spy network in Tsirku.

Archive:Roll of Honour Summer Solstice 3.o: The Roll of Honour for the Summer Solstice 388YE recorded the Imperial citizens who lent their support to named efforts that season, including the Tsirku spy network, the Beacons of Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and forces such as the Citadel Guard, Eastern Sky and Burning Falcon.

Arranging grace.o: At Empress Vesna's request, the Civil Service and Magistrate Abraham appraised the constitutional implications of making the Cat's Graces, a proposed sodality for promoting the arts, an Imperial sodality, while several patron groups offered support if it were approved. The Senate later established the sodality.

Arrows and clay.o: For the Autumn 388YE summit, the heralds of the Iron Duke issued two new challenges to Imperial citizens: a stealth contest among the spider heralds of Jaheris at Widowsglade in Weirmoor, and an art contest with Barien himself as the subject.

As above, so below.o: Six days before the Autumn Equinox 378YE a once-in-a-lifetime Grand Conjunction began, filling the northern night sky with winter lights from Tanikipari in Sermersuaq to Crowslook in Karsk and unsettling magic across the Empire.

As it is when it was.o: A Wind of Fortune gathered mortal and uncertain magical happenings across the Empire as Autumn 386YE approached. They included a winged figure enchanted into Casinea's sky, the completion of Thornsong House, the restoration of the trods, the lifting of Liathaven's curse, the containment of Dho'uala and showy Thule enchantments on their forts.

Asavean Factor.o: In Summer 388YE the Loyalty Assembly, frustrated that only 34 of the 750 wains of white granite needed to Anchor the Way in Asavea had been delivered, sought new ways to advance the project. Several opportunities arose: two competing Synod mandates to find allies, a possible Senate appraisal, and an offer from the eternal Callidus.

Ashes.o: In Summer 386YE the Black Wind sept crossed the Barrens without incident and withdrew into the Mallum. Meanwhile a vast Druj host of seven armies invaded Therunin, conquering Eastring and East Ashes, destroying the Holt of the Oak and the Sarangrave spy network, and laying the Rivers of Life curse over the territory.

Assign Breadbasket Spring 383YE.o: In Spring 384YE the Keeper of the Breadbasket allocated the Bread Basket's surplus to the Marcher territory of Bregasland, in recognition of the sacrifices made by the Marchers and especially by Bregas farmers and citizens.

Assign Spiral.o: In Summer 380YE the Imperial Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Spiral to Urizen, after which Spiral elected a Senator.

Assignment of Holberg.o: In Spring 379YE the Senate voted to allocate the territory of Holberg to the League, choosing it over an alternative proposal to assign it to the Imperial Orcs.

Assignment of Karsk.o: In Spring 378YE the Senate held a procedural vote assigning the newly conquered territory of Karsk to an Imperial nation, and Varushka won it 26 votes to none over the Imperial Orcs.

Assignment of Karsk II.o: In Winter 378YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Karov, allocating the reconquered territory of Karsk to an Imperial nation; Karsk became part of Varushka.

Assignment of Mournwold.o: In Autumn 381YE the Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Mournwold to the Marches.

Assignment of Ossium.o: In Winter 382YE the Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Ossium to the nation of Varushka.

Assignment of Reikos.o: In Winter 379YE the Senate passed a motion assigning Reikos as an Imperial territory under Highguard, allowing it to elect a senator.

Assignment of Segura.o: In Summer 378YE the Senate assigned the newly conquered territory of Segura to the Brass Coast, following an extended military campaign to take it.

Assignment of Skarsind.o: The Senate assigned the conquered territory of Skarsind to the nation of Wintermark in Autumn 377YE, in a procedural vote that passed unanimously.

Assignment of Skarsind II.o: In Autumn 379YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Hahnmark and seconded by Temeschwar, assigning the territory of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs.

Assignment of Spiral Spring 382YE.o: In Spring 382YE the Imperial Senate passed a motion assigning the territory of Spiral to the Urizen nation.

At the dog and eel show.o: In Winter 384YE the yeofolk of the Marches were offered a choice, settled by a tally of votes among farm-holders, between aiding Zenith's recovery, supporting the beaters against a Jotun threat, or tending their own farms for the coming year. Meanwhile around five hundred former Jotun thralls held a secretive gathering at Golden Hoof farm in the Mournwold.

Authorise Ambassador to Axos.o: In Summer 382YE the Senate passed a motion authorising the Ambassador to Axos to invite Axou troops to support the Imperial spy network in the Mountains of the Moon.

Authorise ambassador to Iron Confederacy.o: The Imperial Senate passed a motion authorising the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy to invite Duke Guiscard to send his forces into Feroz to deal with Iron Confederacy rebels and then immediately withdraw.

Authorise targets of the Imperial Guerdo.o: In Winter 380YE the Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies, Dan Brackensong, directed the Imperial Guerdon to the Liathaven Spy Network and three Imperial armies: the Black Thorns, the Hounds of Glory and the Wolves of War.

Authority and acceptance.o: In Autumn 386YE the Empire's foreign relations shifted on several fronts. The Thule agreed to reopen peace treaty talks, Skoura and Tsark planned delegations to Anvil, Asavea put a bounty on shipping trading with the Empire, Jarm pressed its offer over the shield Measure, and the Grendel stayed away.

Axe-bite and ploughshare.o: In Spring 387YE seven Imperial armies marched from the Mournwold into Jotun-held Liathaven, stormed the fortified town of Schogsfestnir and seized Liaven's Glen and Liath's Ring. The Jotun still hold the rest of the territory and are racing to finish a new fortification in West Ranging.

Back in the same place.o: Prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra reported on the Senate's appraisal of a university in Temeschwar to raise the number of commissions the Empire could undertake each season. She set out two opportunities: a new University of Temeschwar creating a League title, the Master of Rings, and an inspirational tomb for Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar creating the Blood Red Builder.

Back in town.o: In late Summer 385YE six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages sent by the Empire's archmages at the Summer Solstice. Zakalwe and Janon offered parleys, Arhallogen called a meeting of uncertain status, Tharim agreed to send courtiers, and Meraud and Prospero made other arrangements.

Bad blood.o: After the magical tempest that broke the drought, the Marcher assembly named the Urizeni magicians behind Thunderous Deluge, but the Constitutional Court treated the Conclave's Concord as an endorsement and ended the magistrates' investigation. Threshers, Highborn magisters and Navarr vates then called on the Senate to create a Conclave-appointed title to lead declarations of sorcery, offering regalia if it acts in time.

Banners and bells.o: Four relic banners hallowed with true liao were created for the Highborn armies, cutting the cost of raising Highguard's fourth army, built around the returning grey pilgrims, to 80 mithril. The page also set out new opportunities for the Highborn Assembly and the Synod's plan to hallow seven bells for a pilgrimage around the Empire.

Battle cries.o: By Summer 385YE the vyig had been broken in the League and Varushka, leaving three desperate bands trying to flee the Empire, each of which could be intercepted through a Sentinel Gate conjunction. The page also covered seized vyig businesses, a proposed Synod mandate honouring the vyig-hunters, and an opportunity to create a League office of the Lantern Wolf.

Beat of your drum.o: The Civil Service's seasonal report on the Commonwealth recorded Militärattache Ludkhannah Schöningen welcoming new Imperial ambassador Finn Pridetalker. It also covered the Lantir War, a one-off mana-for-goods offer, ritual breakthroughs from the Lyceum, the Beurteilung auction, interest in a sungold tablet, Liberty Pact concerns over the Iron Confederacy, and an account of Commonwealth orc spirituality.

Because they must.o: In Autumn 387YE the Tusks and the Burning Falcon conquered the Greensward, storming Farstrider's Watch and the Singing Caves and destroying the last champions loyal to the dead Jarl Haakon. The Mournwold was left entirely in Marcher hands.

Bedight in veils.o: A seasonal round-up of the Empire's dealings with lesser foreign powers: Otkodov, the Iron Confederacy, the Jotun, the Grendel, the people of Tsark, the Karass of the Barrens and the new Protectorate of Morajasse. It covered a newly binding Thule treaty, Thule control of Mieriada, and several diplomatic openings and requests.

Before the sunrise.o: In the run-up to the Spring Equinox 382YE, several strange magical events touched the Empire: a Rivers of Life curse settled over vallorn-haunted Therunin, the Spiral Sword runeforge was completed in Redoubt, and the eternal Irra Harah set bounties on three Imperial citizens. Star-shrouds persisted or appeared over several territories, the Citadel of Fog rose again in Holberg, the Krampus's attackers awaited possible inquisition, and Spiral's cats suffered cursed nightmares.

Beg, steal, or borrow.o: Several traders, envoys and petitioners announced through the Civil Service that they would come to Anvil for the Spring Equinox 382YE, offering or seeking relics, battlefield loot, an antique Freeborn letter, a haunted jar, Feni secrets and bestiary knowledge.

Begin to speak.o: Ahead of the 384YE Summer Solstice, six eternals answered the plenipotentiary messages sent by the Imperial archmages at the Spring Equinox. Jaheris, Roshanwe and Tharim agreed to formal parleys, while Azoth, Estavus and Siakha made other arrangements.

Begins where it ends.o: Ahead of the Winter Solstice 385YE, six eternals answered plenipotentiary messages from the Imperial archmages. Cathan Canae, Surut and Irra Harah agreed to parley, Ephisis replied with offers, Zakalwe and Sadogua declined to meet, and The Azoth requested a parley of its own.

Below the red rock.o: In Spring 386YE the Lasambrian Jotun, reinforced by the Skjalderborn, pressed their invasion of Kahraman, while Isaella's Dance and the Red Wind Corsairs, backed by three magical fortresses in the northern peaks, held them back at heavy cost. The Empire won the battle for Rojota, but the orcs pushed deeper into Gambit and raided the territory's mines.

Below the thunders.o: In Summer 386YE the Imperial armies pressed the Grendel in Madruga's Siroc Plains while a cataclysmic storm, empowered by the eternal Siakha, ravaged the territory. The Empire made two-fifths progress towards claiming the region despite heavy losses on both sides.

Beneath a moonless sky.o: Koskinen, son of one of the Palliko who lead the hylje, invited up to fifty Wintermarkers, explicitly including Steinr and Kallavesa, to the hylje Festival of Autumn's Easing at the coming Autumn Equinox. He also raised three matters to prepare for beforehand: a threat from Fjorknae, an exchange of stories, and hylje help exploring Tsirku.

Beneath mithril spires.o: In Autumn 386YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Commonwealth, the Empire's closest great-power ally. Topics included a new embassy at Hedra, the Commonwealth's war with Jarm, polite opposition to Imperial contact with the Viyerda, a possible Sea of Steel expedition, and Asavean pressure on trade.

Benevolence, inspiration, and legacy.o: In Spring 382YE, Severin von Holberg's General Assembly mandate urging unity around the Seven Virtues was spread across the Empire as a sermon on the signs of Benevolence, Inspiration and Legacy. It damped religious conflict for a year and prompted proposals to curb the National Assemblies and revise the Doctrine of the Paragons.

Best beware my sting.o: The manticore calling itself the Earl of the Groves invited sixteen Dawnish nobles to a feast in the Untrod Groves, where it offered its last favour from Penni the White in a wager of oratory. Separately, some of its yeofolk followers planned to visit Anvil, and the historian Hugh de Veran could be steered towards researching a particular pre-Imperial monarch.

Better world.o: Magician-Prince Barbara Radz of Rigia reformed the treatment of slaves in her principality and demanded the eastern alliance follow. Weeks later Prince Soreana of Borașova and other northern princes began selling beloye zerno, or "white seed", a Jarmish mineral that boosts crystal mana production, to Imperial citizens through the Jarmish traders in Tassato.

Between peace and hate.o: In Winter 382YE, the Empire's orc neighbours stirred on several fronts. The Thule freed Druj-held slaves into Karsk and disputed Sungold Pass, the Great Forest orcs offered intelligence on the Mallum, the Lasambrian Jotun issued an ultimatum over Segura and Feroz, Grendel pirates harried the Bay of Catazar, and the Druj sought a ceasefire with Urizen.

Between stone and salt.o: In Winter 385YE four Imperial armies, the Golden Axe, Towerjacks, Seventh Wave and Winter Sun, marched from Apulian in Spiral into Grendel-held Mareave. They conquered Icarion and Nadir and began pushing into Eoradal.

Between the lines of ages.o: Following the Spring Equinox of 383YE, six eternals (Irra Harah, Sinokenon, the Lictors, Rhianos, Sadogua and Skathe) answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages and agreed to meetings at the Summer Solstice, one of them conditional on amity.

Between two mounds.o: In Autumn 385YE the Jotun sent envoys to the Empire. A ghodi asked the Freeborn's permission to crown the burial mound at Braydon's Jasse with an ever-burning mithril bowl, while in Tromsa the Jarl of Kierheim asked Wintermark's generals to swear that their allies would not despoil the sacred Mount Majastind.

Between wind and water.o: In Winter 383YE, three Dawnish statements of principle from the Autumn Equinox inspired offers to Dawn: a weaver cabal's gifts to award-winning storytellers, a proposed troubadours' chapel in Semmerholm, a proposed manor and fair for knights questing against the vallorn of Brocéliande, and a possible Synod mandate to welcome Marracossan followers of the Way to Astolat.

Beware my power.o: In the run-up to the Winter Solstice of 380YE, a scattering of magical effects was felt across the Empire. Freeborn storms struck the Bay of Catazar, Spring magic rejuvenated Cinion, a new Silver Mask persona emerged, the Semmerlak grew calm, and a hidden conjunction of the Key, Lock and Spider with the Wanderer appeared.

Beyond the light.o: In Winter 383YE, following calls from the Varushkan National Assembly, military units, armies and national assemblies were offered the chance to help secure the newly conquered territory of Ossium. They could do so through wagon raiding, supporting settlers, or venturing into the unknown.

Beyond this dark house.o: In Autumn 384YE, Imperial armies and Thule forces arrived in Ossium to confront the Druj, only to find that the orcs had already withdrawn into the Forest of Ulnak, leaving the Tower of the Scorpion in ruins. The Echofell was quickly brought back under Imperial control, but a Druj sabotage raid in the Drownbark Forest created a new threat.

Bills or bows.o: Following Friar John of the Mourn's Autumn mandate, which urged Marchers to defend their land without drowning it in blood, every Marcher army gained the defensive order to fight shoulder to shoulder, and several Marcher armies were offered new ways to fight during Winter 382YE.

Birds.o: Following two Synod judgements naming the Vale of Gniejezdo in Miekarova as the first shrine of Zoria, the Varushkan Paragon of Wisdom, an opportunity arose to build a great shrine in her honour. During the Summer Solstice the Senate commissioned Zoria's Maze to be transformed into such a shrine.

Birds and bats.o: Two eternals of the Night realm approached the Imperial Conclave: Lashonar announced a love-letter writing contest run by his herald Rossignol, and Sadogua, the Brother of Wizards, sent a herald to request a formal parley. The parley was granted, and shortly after the Winter Solstice the Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith.

Bits and bobs.o: Amid falling Bourse seat prices and dropping wain values, concerned League citizens and the Vigilance Assembly pressed for action on the Empire's finances, and the Civil Service set out options open to the Senate, from publishing the Mint's reports to reallocating Bourse seats, curbing ministries and auctioning sinecures.

Bitter and absolute.o: The Iron Confederacy's Ducal Council declared strict neutrality between the Liberty Pact and the Freedom Accord, refusing to sign either and offering to deal with any nation on an issue-by-issue basis. The Civil Service's seasonal briefing also covered growing Suranni trade through the Brass Coast and a haunted Golden Fleet ship.

Black and white.o: Peter of Hintown's expedition to the Face of Ikka in Sermersuaq, sent to research troll ruins, found a sizeable vein of raw mithril in caves near the great glacier on the border with Tsirku. The Senate went on to commission a mine there.

Blackest night.o: In summer 380YE the nameless red star, now detached from the Wanderer, grew brighter in the northern sky, and every divination agreed it would fall on the Empire, almost certainly somewhere in Miekarova. Meanwhile the starless 'empty skies' spread to new territories and the Phoenix constellation faded almost from sight.

Blood and gold.o: In Summer 382YE, with no Navarr army in Liathaven and the Marcher armies withdrawn, the Navarr faced losing a rare chance to strike at the weakened vallorn. Several proposals arose from recent Navarr and Urizen Assembly judgements to win allies and support for the fight.

Blood and mire.o: In Autumn 386YE six Imperial armies, alongside Navarr warbands, Great Forest Orcs and Knights of Glory, drove the Druj out of Therunin's Lower Tarn Valley and broke most of their hold on Eastring at a terrible cost. The Druj kept East Ashes and the Feverwater Docks and began preparing a magical cataclysm.

Blood makes noise.o: In Spring 384YE, with Synod backing and the support of the Golden Axe and the Hounds of Glory, former Druj slaves joined Varushka and founded new vales across Imperial Ossium. The wind also set out several opportunities: sharing the Crawling Depths, rebuilding the Tower of the Scorpion, the Ketsov claim on the Mir Mozga, an assault on bandit-held Isember, and a Menrothat offer of black lotus.

Blood will thicken.o: Navarr prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater appraised how foreign pilgrims of the Way could be drawn to the Empire. He proposed an artistic contest and a vast folly, the Grand Inspiration of the Way, to remake Bastion's White City into a holy city to supplant Timoj.

Blood-red blooms.o: In Winter 387YE the Grendel armies of the Broken Shore fought the Black Thorns, Argent Sword and Pilgrim's Defiance across Redoubt and took Siluri, adding it to Naris. Imperial magic and cautious tactics stopped them advancing further, and the Imperial armies withdrew in good order to the hills around Cargo.

Bloody murder.o: Four more civil servants of the department of historical research, all studying the origins of the vallorn, were bloodily murdered in the three months after the Spring Equinox 379YE, following earlier killings of their colleagues.

Blossoms a rose in the deeps of my heart.o: The night eternal Janon, the Shadowed Flame, invited the people of the Empire to an audience in the Rosered Woods of Astolat on the third night of the Spring Equinox, opening the regio and chamber there to visitors who came by way of the Sentinel Gate.

Blue flowers in the snow.o: In Winter 385YE Spiral remained divided between the League and Urizen rebels. The Senate funded mana to shroud the spires that chose to stay, while a Winter curse struck Morrow and Redoubt and hardened Urizeni sympathy for the rebels.

Blue seas, white stone.o: Two Asavean trading vessels laden with white granite docked at Sarvos, bringing Alonso Tarquinius, a nobleman and agent of Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones, who intended to visit Anvil during the Summer Solstice. A Plenum warship, rumoured to be rowed by slaves, waited offshore.

Boggarts in Morrow.o: In Winter 378YE boggarts, mana-eating vermin from the realm of Night, infested the Urizen territory of Morrow and threatened its mana sites. The Senate chose to trap the boggarts to reduce the damage to mana production.

Bones in the ocean.o: After the Grendel conquest of the Isle of the Osseini in Feroz, a treaty contract let Freeborn justicars return there, opening opportunities for the Senate to commission a sanctuary for exorcist priests and a fleet-supported spy network. During the Winter Solstice the Imperial Wayleave was used to build that spy network in Feroz.

Born with insight.o: After the General Assembly's mandate against false Virtues passed without a greater majority, its authority was weakened in Urizen, Varushka and Wintermark. This Wind of Fortune set out options for the Varushkan, Wintermark, Vigilance and Wisdom Assemblies to respond.

Both cut alike.o: The Wind of Fortune for the 382YE Summer Solstice listed the conjunctions found by the war scouts and prognosticators. They offered chances to intercept Druj scouts, Jotun warbands, Feni raiders, Grendel pirates and mysterious kidnappers, and to reach Spring regios in Brocéliande and Liathaven.

Briar liar.o: A young Briar calling himself Tobin travelled the Marches spreading false tales that powerful Marcher families had beaten him and tried to drown him, stirring Briars to "fight back". Confronted in Birchland by fifteen-year-old militia member Margary Bolholt, he fled after she was stabbed to death, and he remains at large.

Bricks and boards.o: In Spring 388YE the heralds of Barien, the Iron Duke, announced two challenges for the Spring summit: a tourney of abstract strategy games and a team game of kubb against challengers from the Thule and the Jotun.

Bright yellow blooms.o: At the request of the Navarr Basilisk of the Bourse, the would-be sodality the Rising Tide visited the Canterspire Circle in Operus, Morrow, and proposed ways to spread its Prosperity, chiefly by helping the dye-making Spire of the Golden Wood obtain iridescent gloaming.

Brightness long ago.o: In Autumn 384YE a great expedition of 170 independent captains escorted the koboldi and their red iron door, the Runic Hearth of Adamant, to the bottom of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, sealing the great shaft and ending the threat of a trogoni swarm erupting onto the surface.

Bring you jewels.o: In Winter 387YE Mareave was thriving under the Imperial Orcs: Grendel efforts to retake it had faltered, Ruicraic's Redoubt and the grand aqueduct were complete, and the Golden Pyramid finished its Grand Lodge in Clisearn. Several new commission opportunities were offered across the territory.

Broken arrow.o: After the Wintermark National Assembly's Spring 383YE statements on heroism, opportunities arose for a stealthy Suaq raid on the Jotun-held Pride of Ikka's Tears, a rebuilt aviary at Ishal and a Chronicle of Heroism. In Summer the raid was launched and the Senate commissioned both the aviary and the Chronicle.

Broken sword.o: After the Urizen Assembly repudiated Sulemaine i Taziel, the sword scholar movement split. Loyal scholars, urged by a new mandate, scattered across the Empire, and the unrepentant Disciples of Sulemaine withdrew into the mountains of Zenith.

Budded roses.o: After Dawn's armies drove the Druj back through Semmerholm in a single season and reconquered almost everything lost, a wave of patriotic fervour offered the nation and its Summer allies a series of opportunities. Most were taken up: a national mandate, magical gifts, the Harps of Astolat, the Rose Towers, the Adamant Gate and the Golden Causeway.

Build up my body.o: Following the Assembly of Ambition's endorsement of Ranae de Rondell's mandate to consecrate the Academy of Arms in Redoubt, a wave of interest in Academies of Arms across the Empire created three opportunities: expanding the Siluri Academy into a place of pilgrimage, funding magic items for the Academy in Anvil, and commissioning great works at four other Academies.

Burning.o: In Winter 384YE a Liberty Pact armada sailed from Volkavaar to the Tears of the Moon and destroyed the slave lords' aerie on Rachensgrab, freeing thousands of slaves and shattering the international slave trade.

Bury the hatchet.o: Six eternals (Meraud, the Whisper Gallery, Callidus, Sinokenon, Llofir and Skathe) answered plenipotentiary messages from the Conclave's archmages, each agreeing to a formal parley at the summit. Several set conditions, fixed agendas or requests to meet particular citizens.

Burying the lede.o: A collection of foreign news for Spring 386YE reported that Asavea remained at war with the Empire and was considering more aid to the Grendel. It also covered an Arbonne auction for salvage rights to the sunken Golden Fleet, a Caitun merchant's visit over a slain Sea of Snow kraken, and several diplomatic developments.

Butterfly in reverse.o: After a great Imperial flotilla charted part of the Sea of Snow and reached the Faraden coast, the Faraden of Menendram offered to expand the docks at Caitun if the Empire contributed weirwood and coin. The Senate backed the expansion in Spring 385YE, and the port opened to Imperial fleets after the Autumn Equinox.

By fountains, by fishes.o: In Spring 384YE the Marcher Assembly called its people to raid the Jotun territory of Skallahn after the Spring Equinox, with Wintermark and Navarr pledging to help get raiders in by fishing boat and out overland through Sermersuaq. The Marcher Assembly could choose whether the raid struck military, economic or spiritual targets.

By northern shores.o: The Dawnish army the Gryphon's Pride, acting on an illegal order from General Archavion Wolfborne, marched on the Bitter Strand and seized the Fangs mithril mine from the Rahvin sept, who were legally foreigners under Imperial protection. Imperial captains from every nation fought to defend the orcs, and most of the sept escaped.

Can you hear me?.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages ahead of the 387YE Summer Solstice. Hayaak and Irra Harah agreed to parleys, Janon, Tharim and Kimus sent heralds or emissaries instead, and the City of Locks declined parley but offered meetings, opportunities and a market.

Can't give everything away.o: Having seen the Free Seas Pact founder without Imperial backing, the Sarcophan Delves declared the Pax Sarcophan in Summer 387YE. They threatened war on any nation that blockades neutral trade or sponsors piracy, which led Asavea to withdraw its bounty on ships visiting the Empire.

Carnival of rust.o: In Spring 384YE seven Imperial armies, including the Dawnish Eastern Sky and three Highborn armies, invaded Druj-held Zenith again and took roughly half of Clypion. The Citadel Guard's Autumn magic trapped the Druj armies in a Glass Labyrinth, while the Druj unleashed tormented Urizen sentinels and planned to poison the Proceris marshes.

Carved in stone.o: Broken oaths sworn by members of the Assembly of Nine to bear auras of Peace brought a year-long curse of discord on the Wisdom and Prosperity assemblies, while Viviane Barossa's steadfast keeping of her vow strengthened the Vigilance Assembly. The Empire also gained the opportunity to build the Forge of Bonds, an oathing place at the Fingers in Hahnmark.

Castle of wind and sky.o: Cathan Canae, the Summer eternal known as the Mistress of Blizzards, placed a curse on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, the new magical college at the edge of the vale of Volchitrava, assailing anyone who leaves the castle with snow and targeted gales. The college kept working, but its upkeep doubled because of the higher wages needed to persuade magicians to come.

Cede Trajadoz.o: The Senate passed a motion in Winter 384YE ceding the town of Trajadoz in Madruga to the Marracossan exiles, former Asavean citizens who fled to the Empire after the short-lived Asavean civil war. It also created a new Brass Coast national position, the Marracossa Sendito.

Cede region of Misericorde to Sand Fishe.o: In Spring 383YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Holberg's senator and seconded by Karsk's, ceding the region of Misericorde in Holberg to the Sand Fishers, an orc nation based in Ossium.

Chain and anchor.o: In Spring 388YE the Sarcophan Delves stayed friendly to the Empire and keen on trade, but reset several dealings. The Alivetti estate's five-year celebration ended without Highborn attendance, the Kruidenkenner withdrew most offers, and the Highborn stone boom ended. An entrepreneur offered to buy the Cathedral of the Navigators.

Chain around my leg.o: In Winter 381YE the Winter Sun, resting in Casinea under an enchantment meant to help orcs hear their ancestors, were flooded with the angry voices and visions of orcs once enslaved by the Empire. The army's general, Bloodcrow Morg'ur, then paid 25 wains of weirwood to permanently remake the army as Freedom Fighters.

Chains from the deep.o: After the Vigilance Assembly upheld a Writ of Consecration for the Great Chain of Sarvos, an opportunity arose to consecrate it with true liao from the Sun Chamber, opening the way to a new cathedral, expanded defences and a spiteful offer from Skathe.

Change.o: In Spring 382YE the eternals Murit and Soghter ceased to exist and a new Night eternal, Azoth, claimed to be their alchemical recreation. Mines and forests across the Empire began yielding strange, random materials, and the regio and works tied to the old eternals were transformed.

Change to Imperial Breadbasket.o: In Winter 381YE the Keeper of the Imperial Breadbasket, Rowan Merrick, redirected the Breadbasket away from supporting the Mournwold and towards the upkeep of the Citadel Guard army, a change that passed.

Changing of the guards.o: After Empress Lisabetta won the tourney to become Monarch of Dawn and the Dawnish National Assembly declared her the ultimate authority in Dawn, two Dawnish movements sought Synod mandates: one to make her Queen in truth, the other to place glory above virtue.

Chaos, and the stillness of it.o: The vallorn heart in Brocéliande grew stronger again in Spring 383YE, doubling the force needed to hold back its spread into Boar's Dell and Elerael and to save the steading of the Broch. Elsewhere, the Jotun invaded Liathaven and the Feni raiding Hercynia vanished.

Charter Sarcombe market town.o: In Winter 381YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Mournwold and seconded by Sermersuaq, granting an Imperial Charter that recognises Sarcombe in the Mournwold as a market town.

Chasing you home.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 385YE, prognosticators identified two major conjunctions on the Saturday morning, one to the Morogvejo valley in Kahraman and one to Graven Rock in Bregasland. The Military Council was to choose between them, and which nations would take part, at the Friday muster.

Children in bloom.o: In Spring 385YE the Brass Coast's Sails of the First Flame cast the Hallow of the Green World, flooding the Empire with Spring magic. It brought flowers, fertility and healing herbs, but also wild side effects, including serious damage to the Empire's roads.

Children of Wrecks.o: Followers of Siakha in the Bay of Catazar formed a loose coalition, the Children of Wrecks, under High Priestess Shivaarn, broke decisively from the Grendel and claimed Free Landing and Cazar Straits. Several conjunctions arose to confront them or to exploit savage raids they had inspired.

Chilled to the bone.o: In autumn 382YE, Dawnish and Varushkan armies invaded Ossium in the Mallum, catching the Druj by surprise. They captured the Crawling Depths mithril mine and the Bitter Vats, freed slaves, and met the territory's orc and human inhabitants.

Chime the sound.o: After the Thule Dragons outlawed slavery and the Senate lifted tariffs on Thule trade, the Thule offered the Imperial Orcs two knowledge-for-reward exchanges. Meanwhile the Brass Coast was given the chance to send charitable food to a hungry Otkodov, or to send priests north at the risk of a diplomatic incident.
