Meanwhile a vallornspawn horde led by a cultist dubbed Shadowspore invaded Mareholm, presenting the Empire with linked conjunctions of which only one could be used.

Some kind of trouble.o: For the Spring Equinox 384YE summit, the civil service's prognosticators published the Sentinel Gate conjunctions they had identified, ranging from major battles against the Jotun, Yegarra and Druj to smaller missions against the vallorn, spy operations and rescues.

Some to misery are born.o: Marcher refugees from Whittle settled in a two-street enclave in Tassato Mestra, where their open reverence for Hatred as a virtue drew growing concern from the League and Marcher assemblies of the Synod. Two possible Synod mandates were set out for denouncing or shunning them.

Something must break.o: In Autumn 383YE a conjunction of the Wanderer, the Great Wyrm, the Drowned Shepherd and the Claw, read as favouring transformation over endings, gave Urizen a chance to recast the Citadel Guard's cyclic magic. It also marked the founding of the Grand Library of Canterspire and Urizen Lore, and opened Synod opportunities to endorse cooperation with eternals.

Song of the lakefolk.o: A growing band of strange, skin-clad spear-hunters calling themselves companions of the Ætheling of Atkonaroq camped on the northern shore of Lake Atkonaroq in Sermersuaq and began raiding nearby halls, searching for something but taking nothing. The Assembly of Wisdom chose to have the locals gather information, sending Savik Summerstorm to lead the effort.

Songs like trees.o: In Autumn 387YE the Golden Sun and the Wolves of War, joined by well over a hundred independent captains, marched from Reikos into Therunin and held back a vallorn surge in Peakedge Song. They arrived to find that the Druj had burned Peakedge Stead after Lord Rain withdrew his protection and turned away from the Empire.

Sorrow and death.o: After a riot at the Spire of Twisting Shadows in Lustri, Zenith, two magical threats spread across the territory: the escaped patient Nazares Praesidio raised a growing legion of husks, and a Winter curse of sorrow spread from Lustri. Both were ended by the Summer Solstice.

Sound and vision.o: In Summer 387YE a wide range of magical events swept the Empire. Jaheris paid performers to spread a comic poem about General Gabriel Barossa, Winterfolk mystics found a way to bind the artok Little Icebarn, and Mount Polus rose in Zenith. Plans emerged to reach the Lyceum again, the Conclave interdicted the Claw's blood magic, and Falconer cultists and coral husks threatened several territories.

Sound the bells.o: In Spring 386YE, curses born of the feud between Urizen and the Marches battered the Empire: Icy Maw halved mana production across Urizen and drove up mana prices, while Foam and Spittle storms lashed the northern Bay of Catazar against the Grendel. The storms flooded Sarvos, strained foreign trade and stranded Grendel crews in Necropolis.

Sowing on the mountains.o: In Winter 381YE a week-long storm battered the mountains between Volodmartz and Otkodov, and its floods and landslides uncovered four building opportunities: an ancient ossuary in Miekarova and three finds in Volodmartz.

Speak to me.o: Six eternals answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary messages after the Winter Solstice. Skathe, Cathan Canae, Sadogua and Ossegrahn arranged meetings for the Spring Equinox, while the Invisible Hand and Ylenwe chose to act directly instead.

Spear of the stars.o: With Dogri Thulebane captured and Crow's Keep ruined, the Thule extended cautious friendship to the northern Empire through their envoy Rak. They offered a trade link, an ambassadorship and a deal over Gildenheim's relics, while Wintermark pressed demands over slaves and murdered Winterfolk.

Splitting the pot.o: In Spring 384YE the Bounders sealed off the Mournwold village of Whittle so that only Marchers could try its Hatred sect. When the villagers refused to surrender, a brutal battle left most of them dead, and the sect's enclave in Tassato was broken up.

Spreading the Way.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest delivered a civil service appraisal on bringing non-Wayist cultures within the Empire into the Way of Virtue. She concluded that no general answer or commission was possible, and instead offered three broad approaches and urged the Empire to appraise specific groups with simple goals.

Spreading the word.o: Accounts of Past-Life Visions, gathered by a team of Torchbearers under Livia Cascade, the Seer of the Gateway, were published across the Empire by the Spider's Vantage Spire, a publishing-house in Redoubt. It was the first such publication in living memory, and possibly the first since Nicovar's purge.

Stand amid the roar.o: In Autumn 387YE the Narwhal's Spear, the Sun Chamber and pilgrims answering the Wintermark and Highborn assemblies moved against the Cult of the Falconer in Sermersuaq, shattering its forces and uncovering a plan to mark the territory with the power of the Claw using four buried white granite obelisks.

Stand proud, you're strong.o: After the Freeborn National Assembly raised its highest calling to defend the nation's borders, the hakima identified over a dozen ways to strengthen the Brass Coast's defences, of which the Assembly could pursue up to four over the following year. Freeborn armies were also inspired to take a ferocious new defensive order in Freeborn-held territories.

Standards.o: In Summer 386YE the Jotun armies the Lion of the North and the Tower of the North marched out of Liathaven and conquered three-fifths of Southmoor in the Mournwold, storming the market town of Sarcombe and driving out its Marcher and Highborn defenders.

Standing in the sun.o: Highguard extended its peerless kinship to the Imperial Orcs, helping the six septs in Skarsind work together in virtue and setting out proposals for each sept. In response the Senate funded miners for the Black Forge, assemblies backed a Bone Pilgrimage, the Feldspar Distillery was built and Gildenheim was walled.

Starfall.o: In Autumn 380YE the red star known as the Stalker began its final descent, set to strike Miekarova during the Autumn Equinox unless ritual magic diverted it. Showers of shooting stars scattered ilium-bearing fragments across the north.

Stars and sigils.o: In Spring 387YE a series of magical and uncanny events swept the Empire. Maddened beasts and sudden violence spread from Sermersuaq, a Varushkan village was slaughtered in Ossium, and a Grand Conjunction of the Great Wyrm and the Mountain unravelled warlike magic while empowering other enchantments.

Start a fire.o: After the Navarr and their Marcher allies drove the vallorn back from West Ranging in Liathaven, the vates declared the vallorn weakened, opening a rare chance to attack and reclaim the Westwood before the Winter Solstice.

Start a war.o: In the aftermath of the Gryphon's Pride's night assault on the Rahvin at the Fangs, Dawn split between Gryphons backing General Archavion Wolfborne and Unicorns condemning the attack. The Senate had to decide the fate of the captured mithril mine.

Starting at the end.o: The Civil Service presented the Senate with a set of surveyed infrastructure opportunities across the Empire: the Iron Roads of Varushka, beacons and watchtowers in Wintermark, a highway, causeway and canal in the Marches, and new roads in the Brass Coast. The Senate later approved the Wintermark beacons in Autumn 382YE and the Iron Roads in Autumn 383YE.

Statement of Intent regarding the Stalke.o: In Summer 380YE the Senate passed in principle a statement of intent, as part of the ongoing peace treaty with the Thule, to accept their gesture of goodwill and use a Thule ritual to divert the Stalker comet to the Thule territory of Sküld.

Steel and salt.o: In Autumn 386YE the Golden Axe, Winter Sun and Seventh Wave marched south from Mareave into Ayereed and met the Grendel in the Petrified Forest, pushing them back until the Empire was almost halfway to conquering the region.

Stings like the truth.o: In Summer 382YE the Whisper Gallery's agents kept targeting Imperial scholars, a Highborn chapter campaigned to curb the Seer of the Gateway, Livia Cascade, and the eternal Sung grew displeased with the Empire over some spoiled mystery.

Stone and stone.o: In Winter 383YE Adamant's koboldi presented a series of proposals for unique structures that only the newly created Master of the Koboldi could commission, from a residence for the Archmage of Summer to great statues, an adamant-reinforced fortress and a door to seal the trogoni-infested sinkhole.

Strange allies.o: In Summer 379YE Lasambria was invaded twice, by the Jotun from the north and the Iron Confederacy from the south, and Lasambrian, Suranni and Jotun envoys all sought to sway the Senate. The Jotun warned that any Imperial aid to the Lasambrians would end their ceasefire with the Empire.

Strange fruit.o: Following two Synod judgements of the 379YE Winter Solstice, the efforts of Elka Nadyanova Gremani and Duke Ferrero bore fruit: the Hierro clan of Lasambrian refugees genuinely and widely embraced the Virtues. This left open the question of what the Empire would now do with them.

Strange harvest.o: In Autumn 379YE, vallorn miasma and ettercap raids spilled from Brocéliande into Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm, followed by a wave of Spring magic that twisted a quarter of farm and forest produce. Among the aberrations grew thorny bushes whose fruit yields seed pods usable as Spring mana.

Struggle with the sea.o: With the first phase of the Grendel peace treaty concluded, Governor Rahab sealed the borders of Feroz after a Brass Coast mandate drove a torrent of Freeborn to flee west, and the Empire was offered the chance to mount a covert land and sea evacuation of those left behind.

Summer in Winter.o: In Winter 379YE a harsh winter gripped Varushka, but a potent Summer enchantment settled across Miekarova, Karov, Volodmartz and Karsk, stirring Varushkans to confront the dark forces around them, usually with happy outcomes.

Summer tree.o: In Autumn 384YE the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher's forces completed the conquest of Bregasland, taking The Rushes and Gravenmarch. The Strong Reeds stayed in the marshes, working with the renegade House Greywater to harry the invaders.

Sun green.o: The Summer 383YE Wind of Fortune reported on the Empire's magic. Stars vanished over Druj-linked territories, Thule veiled its lands, and magical castles were raised in Spiral, Semmerholm and Bregasland. The Three Watchers were carved in Morrow, and several eternals made offers to the Conclave.

Sunrise over Livardz.o: Following a Senate motion by Ostrik Vulpe, prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra identified three challenges to restoring the prosperity of Livardz in Volodmartz, left ruined by Cold Sun's Shepherds of Ash: rebuilding the vales, removing the silent menace, and breaking the curse of the ashen wind.

Support Expansion of Caitun.o: In Spring 385YE the Senate passed a motion to support the Faraden expansion of their port of Caitun, providing 15 wains of weirwood and 45 crowns in transport costs, so that Imperial fleets could trade there and hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow.

Support medical school and Anvil hospita.o: In Spring 377YE the Senate passed a motion to fund, found and recognise an Imperial school of medicine and a hospital in Anvil. It was proposed by the Senator for Bregasland and seconded by the Senator for Sarvos.

Survival.o: The Sun Chamber's appraisal, aided by Vainakoma Dawnstongue, examined how to protect Imperial infrastructure from vallorn expansion. It concluded that armies and fortifications remain the main answer, but identified several new opportunities.

Swans will sing.o: In Winter 379YE, resentment in Wintermark over the peace treaty that ceded the Stonefield Ice Caves to the Thule created an opportunity for the Wintermark national assembly to urge illegal raids across the border into Thule lands. The assembly passed no judgement, and the opportunity lapsed.

Swords and sorcery.o: After driving the Druj from Semmerholm and conquering Ossium, Dawn's war fervour, stoked by Pelleas Thorne's mandate, opened three limited opportunities at the Winter Solstice 382YE. The Hounds of Glory became an army of indomitable glory, and the Senate approved enlarging the Golden Sun.

Symposium of Revelation.o: At the Winter Solstice of 380YE the Synod held the Symposium of Revelation in Anvil, a public programme of sermons, panels and debates organised by the Marcher Symposiarch Edward Watcher of King's Stoke to address recent upheavals in the Imperial Faith. Foreign priests and delegations, including some from nations at war with the Empire, were invited to attend.

Take it further.o: After a disappointing Spring raid on Skallahn that lacked the strength to achieve lasting harm, the Empire was offered the chance to launch a second, better-planned raid in Summer 384YE. The Jotun were overconfident and had not yet shored up their defences.

Taken at the flood.o: In Summer 385YE the Imperial armies drove the scattered Druj from most of the Barrens, conquering the Bleaks, the Untrod Groves and Farweald, while a storm of Druj curses brought floods, murderous trees and Winter spirits across the territory.

Tale of the Golden Hare.o: After the Varushkan assembly declared the executed members of the Tangled Thorns coven good and virtuous Varushkans, people across Varushka, especially in Miekarova, began adopting the golden hare as a symbol. The Varushkan national assembly then mandated that the hare is a symbol of Ambition.

Tales of imagination.o: In Summer 386YE a series of eternal-driven opportunities reached the Empire, including access for heroes to the Four Corners Fair, Cathan Canae's offer of a third ritual to Wintermark and Azoth's readiness to help the Navarr reattune the last singing stone. Further items covered Sanvar Isk's Loom auction, Janon's Shadowed Torchbrand, Sadogua's offers, a debate contest, Barien's planned tourney and Lashonar's call for letters of longing.

Tales of mystery.o: A Summer 386YE Wind of Fortune gathered several magical mysteries across the Empire. They included the Deadwood Knight's attack on the Earl of Fools' estate, a Three Sisters curse on Freeborn hakima, an unseen beast stalking Kalpaheim, an inspiring enchantment over Miaren and a strange affliction at a Navarr steading.

Talk softly.o: In Summer 382YE the Great Forest Orcs, recovered and settled in Therunin, asked for formal Imperial or Navarr permission to travel the trods with Navarr stridings. Meanwhile the Thule prepared a final round of peace talks amid troop build-ups, and the Grendel rejected peace while ceding Spiral to the Empire.

Talking sailor.o: Grendel pirates, emboldened by their control of the Bay of Catazar and backed by heralds of the eternal Siakha, began preying more heavily on Imperial trading ships. The Senate was offered two responses, flying foreign colours or funding a map of the Bay, and it voted to map the Bay.

Talking to friends.o: In Summer 387YE the Asavean Plenum, humbled by the Pax Sarcophan and its naval defeat at Zemeh, signalled that it was open to ending its war with the Empire if Imperial missionaries stopped preaching the Way in the Archipelago. Meanwhile the Sumaah Republic, grateful for Imperial help against the Asavean armada, began sending true liao each season but refused to work jointly on anchoring the Way in Asavea.

Tears in the rain.o: After Dawnish and Navarr forces liberated Reikos from the Druj in Winter 379YE, this Wind of Fortune set out the state of the ravaged territory and the opportunities for rebuilding it. Everything depended on the Senate deciding which nation the territory would be assigned to.

Temple of the bull.o: With Senate permission, Asavean priests began building a grand temple to Balo of the Foam and the Black Bull at the port of Oran in Feroz. The Assembly of Nine denounced it as idolatry, and Abaddon de Rondell's preaching delayed its completion until shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

Ten travellers tales.o: Ahead of the 385YE Autumn Equinox, word spread of several groups of visitors bound for Anvil. They included Axou traders and scholars, three orc septs ready to pledge themselves to the Imperial Orcs, Thule warlocks, a Jotun ghodi, new orc citizens of Tassato, a Commonwealth philosopher and self-declared former Asaveans.

Tend to the Flame.o: In Winter 383YE the Silent Bell's covert investigation of Whittle gave the Cardinal of Vigilance the names of the leaders of a sect of Hatred, and the Synod went on to condemn twelve Whittlefolk for blasphemy and heresy. The wind also covered the Mournwold thralls' future, bandits preying on them, and Marcher fears over the Rivers Run Red interdiction.

Tested again and again.o: Debate sparked by Severin von Holberg's sermon turned in Autumn 382YE to the Synod's relationship with the Military Council, Conclave, Bourse and Senate. Several priests and scholars put forward proposals that would need Senate motions to enact, while the lingering effect of the sermon blunted some potential religious conflicts.

That's where my heart is.o: Emperor Vesna delivered an Imperial address in Summer 387YE, written on the road to war against the Druj. In it Vesna endorsed the Synod's stance against false virtue, urged all citizens to reject false virtues, and began a practice of commending exceptional citizens.

The Ambition of Thrace.o: Following a Synod writ of consecration honouring Thrace, Exemplar of Ambition, the civil service identified the Legion's Rookery in Gildenheim, Skarsind, as the ideal site for an inspirational location to his memory. Consecrating it requires a General Assembly mandate and a dose of true liao at the Spring Equinox.

The Courageous Priest.o: In spring 380YE the Courage of the First Empress, a movement inspired by the preaching of Golan the Wanderer and of Yael of Felix's Watch, who claims to be the First Empress reborn, took root across Highguard. Citizens abandoned other virtues for congregations of Courage, and the Synod's own preacher, Nina of Cantiarch's Hold, could not stem the tide.

The DOOM that came to Sarvos.o: After the Hag Queen's agents shattered every mirror in Sarvos at the Summer Solstice 383YE, the Jewelled City lost its famous identity. The League was offered a chance to choose a new future for the city through Senate commissions, or else risk Sarvos becoming 'doomed'.

The Deer in the Sun.o: Following Cold Sun's destruction of cultural sites, the Imperial Orc and Varushkan Assemblies called for new monuments to national Pride (a Library of Worth in Skarsind and a Hall of Fabric Arts in Karov), while the Navarr Assembly urged its people to fight the scions. Mandates supporting all three passed, but neither building had yet been commissioned by the Senate.

The Glorious Advance.o: After the Red Wind Corsairs, Eastern Sky and Hounds of Glory drove the Lasambrians out of Segura, patriotic fervour in Dawn and the Brass Coast created a short-lived chance to raise a new army or navy more cheaply. The Assembly of Pride chose to celebrate the Brass Coast, and the resulting enthusiasm helped muster the Freeborn Storm navy.

The Net of the Realms.o: After the Urizen National Assembly upheld Maximillian's mandate urging cooperation with eternals, several Urizeni came forward with offers from Meraud, Zakalwe, Prospero, Sung, Sadogua and the Whisperer to aid the nation. The Whisperer's offer to bring the Dream of Famine on an enemy territory was put before the Conclave but withdrawn without a vote.

The Oran operation.o: In Summer 388YE, Protectorate of Morajasse engineers, guided by Lutomysla Niegoslava, assessed how to reconnect Feroz and Madruga across the flood-ravaged Scorrero. They proposed an Oran Bridge across the Bay of Oran as a commission opportunity, along with optional salvage and toll arrangements.

The Pride of Gerallt Brackensong.o: Following a Pride assembly writ of consecration for the Navarr exemplar Gerallt Brackensong, the civil service presented three possible sites for a consecrated memorial school and garden, leaving the General Assembly to choose one by mandate at the Spring Equinox.

The Prosperity of Good Walder.o: In response to a Prosperity assembly writ of consecration, the civil service proposed three sites in the Marches for an inspirational location dedicated to the paragon Good Walder. These were Good Walder's Orchard and the Abbey of Harry's Pot in Mitwold, and Corwin's Thump in Upwold. The General Assembly was invited to choose one at the Spring Equinox.

The Queen's door.o: Eleonaris, the Lion of Summer, remained enraged at the Empire's repeated use of Knights of Glory without public thanks, and the civil service identified four commissions that could placate her: a folly at Semmer's Rose, or a fane at the Giltmere, Oremont or the Semmerstones.

The Synod speaks.o: After the Navarr Assembly chose to begin the final war against the vallorn, the Assembly of Nine and the League and Varushkan Assemblies backed them with greater majorities. The League and Varushka were each offered competing mandates to commit their people to the fight.

The Visitation.o: In Summer 388YE several visitors and matters publicly bound for Anvil were announced. They included a disputed salvage delivery delayed by stewards from Oreb's Vault, a mysterious letter from the City of Bar and Bond, a rock, paper, scissors tournament run by Landskeeper Shem of Upwold, and a visit by Wayblade Skana of Mareave.

The Witches of Applefell.o: Witch-supported bandits, apparently operating from around the Dawnish hill town of Applefell in Weirwater, stole five wains of weirwood from a caravan of the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat. The magistrates have met a wall of silence from the townsfolk.

The arch of the door.o: With the Druj advancing through Morrow, the Academy abandoned its offices at Canterspire and began moving to new buildings near the Castle of Thorns in Dawn. The move left the Dean of Pilgrims title without purpose, and the civil service offered the Senate two ways to redefine it; the opportunity later lapsed and the title is no longer active.

The art of restraining power.o: The Autumn 381YE foreign-relations Wind of Fortune covered the Empire's neighbours. Sumaah recognised the orc priests Bonewall Rek and Cole, Axou priests lectured across the Empire, Faraden hailed a planned trade hub in Upwold, and the Thule warlock Skogr the Red freed fifty Imperial slaves under a ransom agreement.

The best soil.o: Following the Marcher Assembly's Autumn Equinox 385YE mandate welcoming the former Jotun thralls, the Mournwold Orcs began joining the Marches as citizens, despite their heretical belief in reincarnation. The Doctrine of Enlightenment eased the way, and the change opened the possibility of a fifth Marcher army.

The bird and the child.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 384YE, eternals of all six realms answered the Imperial archmages' plenipotentiary invitations, and Sinokenon unusually requested a parley with the Archmage of Day without having been invited.

The blessing way.o: In Autumn 383YE the Empire's dealings with several orc nations shifted: the Sand Fishers flourished in Misericorde under Imperial support until a Druj invasion of Holberg terrified them, while the Jotun rebuffed an embassy, the Thule began honouring their treaty and a Grendel envoy came to Anvil.

The bones of what you believe.o: Following Navarr Synod mandates, the Empire was offered the chance to expand the Great Library of Hacynian into a true repository of Navarr lore whose study, once built, would reveal a way to destroy the vallorn. The wind also proposed a Hall of the Seven in Miaren and reported two vates captured by Druj on the Feverwater.

The brightest flame.o: In Summer 388YE the Highborn Assembly extended peerless kinship to the Brass Coast, sending pilgrims to Anduz to debate the resurgent firebrands. The visit revealed much about the movement but did nothing to change it, and it produced a proposal for a Highborn bathhouse in Anduz.

The circle game.o: In Winter 387YE the prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra delivered the Senate's appraisal of trades that ministries could make without coin. She found few options and instead examined the Imperial treasury's declining revenues, setting out ways to abrogate or convert ministries and listing great works that would draw more money into the Anvil economy.

The cities and the city.o: In Autumn 385YE the Grendel spy ring in Necropolis was broken, a second ring was found in Sarvos, work began on the Grand Inspiration in Bastion under the threat of Cold Sun, and the Winter Sun sought items of worth in Necropolis. Varushkan wise ones were refused entry to Empress Varkula's tomb, and Synod mandates were offered to armies advancing into the Salt Flats of Sanath.

The city asleep.o: In Autumn 384YE heralds of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea, offered the Empire a dying Cauldron of Gold whose food protects against the vallorn miasma. They invited heroic bands to a grand adventure from the Broch in Brocéliande into the heart of ruined Terunael.

The city below.o: With the Urizeni rebellion in Ankra and Cinion largely stabilised, attention turned to the fast-growing city of Apulian in Spiral. The League chose to embrace Urizeni culture there, and Urizen agreed to share the secrets of the mithril Block that protects minds from the Black Plateau.

The concisest tenant.o: In Winter 387YE Temeschwar's rat plague had been largely tamed by the Rat Kings guild, while the dramaturgical figure of the Doctor, especially in rat-masked form, began lending magical strength to the city. Two rival proposals also emerged to remodel Virtue's Respite, the former tomb of Empress Giselle.

The cry of gulls.o: In Spring 386YE five Imperial armies, the Freeborn Fire of the South and Burning Falcon with the Marcher Bounders, Drakes and Strong Reeds, counter-attacked the Grendel in Madruga. They held Calvos and liberated Lightsea at heavy cost, while the Siakha cult of High Priestess Shivaarn seized Free Landing and claimed the whole Bay of Catazar.

The current when it serves.o: In Summer 385YE the Bloodcloaks, the Green Shield and the Summer Storm invaded Jotun-held Skallahn from Stark, conquering Greenwall and fighting halfway through Iron Stand. Meanwhile Blade Quencher's Hall, an Autumn fane allied to the Jotun, began expanding and disgorging Estavus' warriors.

The darkest road.o: In Autumn 384YE Imperial armies retook Zenith, holding Clypion and Iteri while the Hounds of Glory seized Lustri at heavy cost, trapping seven Druj armies in Proceris and Occursion. The page also sets out a major battle at the Glade of Night Enshrouding and six linked conjunctions across the territory.

The day writes the words.o: The contest between Dawn and the Imperial Orcs for the Barrens divided the Synod. Civil servants also found that the Barrens orcs are too hostile to the Empire to rise against the Druj for ten years, and several ways were offered to shape the campaign and shorten that wait.

The dead tree gives no shelter.o: In Autumn 379YE several thousand Lasambrian orcs of the Hierro army, the Empire's recent allies, crossed from Reinos into Segura with their non-combatant families. They camped near Anduz and sent a delegation to Anvil to ask for Imperial support.

The deepest cut.o: After the Urizen Assembly backed Herminius of the House of the Wanderer's plan to consecrate the newly found tomb of Sulemaine i Taziel in Peregro with true liao, this Wind of Fortune set out how such an inspirational tomb could be created and what each choice of virtue would mean. Sulemaine has never been recognised as an exemplar or paragon by the Synod.

The divide between.o: In Winter 382YE the Empire faced competing appeals over the revolt of the Asavean satrapies of Marracoss and Emphedor: the Asavean Plenum sought continued support, while the rebel leader Terentia Comasigne petitioned for aid. The Senate resolved the question by making it legal for Imperial mercenaries to fight for either side.

The dose makes the poison.o: In Autumn 388YE the Golden Axe of Varushka marched from the Bleaks into the poisoned Lower Tarn Valley of Therunin, broke the Druj warlord Egrech's stronghold at Razorhill and claimed the region for the Empire. They lost perhaps three hundred soldiers, mostly to the lingering poison of the Sephals Cauldron.

The falling sky.o: A spring 385YE round-up of the Empire's foreign relations: the Liberty Pact summit collapsed after Axos boycotted it, Grendel raiders burned the docks at Issyk, and rumours spread of an Asavean surprise attack on the Imperial coast. Elsewhere the Sarcophan Delves warmed further to the Empire.

The fate of the many.o: After the Senate assigned Spiral to the League, the territory's Urizeni inhabitants reacted with anger, relief and grief, and looked to the Urizen National Assembly for a plan. The Wind also brought offers from two eternals of Night, Sadogua and Sung.

The fayre fight.o: In Autumn 386YE Dawn marked the end of the Grand Tour at Anvil with a final tourney among its most dedicated competitors, a yeofolk fayre in the Glory Square, the Knight-protector of Autumn tourney and a debate over the Challenger in Waiting. Rhydian de Rondell won the final contest, and the Senate made the Challenger in Waiting an appointment of the Dawnish Assembly.

The final countdown.o: Following calls from the Navarr and Highborn Assemblies to act on newly discovered knowledge of how to destroy the vallorn, the Navarr and Highguard were asked to decide whether to begin the final war against it. Both nations chose to commit: the Navarr in Summer 386YE and the Highborn in Autumn 386YE.

The first shot.o: After the Navarr Assembly voted by greater majority (464-18) at the Summer Solstice 386YE to begin the final war against the vallorn, many Navarr stridings left the trods and returned home. The nation gained the capacity to raise three new armies in Hercynia, Therunin and Miaren.

The flood and the storm.o: In Winter 381YE the six-month silence of Spring-aligned regio ended abruptly in a surging flood of Spring magic, empowering Imperial magicians at a cost and creating short-lived opportunities to build structures in Hahnmark, Redoubt and Miaren. The Senate chose to build Seren's Whispering Garden in Miaren.

The gathering storm.o: In Autumn 386YE the Military Council learned, via the Grendel spymaster Sea-Wraith, that the Children of Wrecks were massing on the Freeborn Plain outside Atalaya in Free Landing, where four captains planned to bind their fleets into a navy. Imperial forces were offered objectives to stop the navy and a favoured coven, and to recover two valuable items.

The greatest city in the world.o: Holberg won the League's year-long contest to see which city spent most on commissions and improvements, and the resulting surge of civic Pride brought opportunities to deepen Holfried's defences, turn Holmauer into a garden city, and exploit a newly discovered weirwood grove in Misericorde. Work also began on Empress Lisabetta's memorial in the Necropolis.

The greatest plurality.o: After the Archbishop of Capodomus's sermon, the Synod's General Assembly failed to unite behind a single great Ambition for the Empire, splitting its votes between the Druj, the vallorn, Asavea and other goals. This prompted two competing proposed mandates on assembly authority and new donations of wains and money to the Virtue fund.

The hammer and the anvil song.o: Over the Winter Solstice 383YE, several visitors brought trade opportunities to Anvil, including a narcotics market, a crafts exchange, an auction of invitations to Basileus Flint's game, the sale of a sword from the Freedom Heresy and an offer of Summer talismans for beggar's lye. The Bourse's weirwood seats and several national titles were also up for appointment.

The hard way.o: After the true consecration of Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, Archbishop Estella Lucati preached a sermon on Ambition urging the Empire to commit itself to destroying the vallorn. It offered the General Assembly a mandate to make the vallorn the Empire's overriding goal, at the price of neglecting the Druj and the Asaveans.

The honey offering.o: In Spring 383YE a wave of Varushkan ambition, spurred by Bartimaeus's mandate and Winter Synod judgements, produced several proposals to restore the nation's wealth: buying back the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, rebuilding the Iron Roundtower, resettling freed refugees in Karsk and reviving the Iron Roads. The Varushkan national assembly endorsed a mandate urging its people to prosper through mines and forests.

The horror and the wild.o: After the Varushkan National Assembly urged its people to seek out and bargain with the dark powers of their lands, Varushkans struck private deals that brought strange windfalls and terrible prices. The results included three commission opportunities, continued trouble from the sovereign Dho'uala on the Semmerlak, and two dangerous conjunctions in northern Weirwater.

The illusion of majesty.o: In Spring 383YE several opportunities came to the Empire ahead of the summit: the eternal Estavus offered doubled rewards for ambergelt, while a Holberg bandit-hunting company, an Autumn card game, a struggling Marcher bakery, a mysterious Urizen bracelet and a herald of Lashonar each sought Imperial attention.

The keys of blood.o: In Summer 388YE several eternals approached the Empire with threats, offers and opportunities. These included Janon's heralds threatening to curse Ossium and Sarangrave, a Grendel defector in Kallavesa, Agramant's illegal aid to Navarri in Therunin, and Rhianos's request for the Tourney Grounds of Laroc.

The lake and the deep, dark woods.o: In Winter 385YE Dho'uala, the dark sovereign of the Semmerlak, lost patience with the Empire after being denied her due and continued to take her tithe from the lake. Meanwhile the undying Deadwood Knight, or Schlacta of Rot, failed to return to slumber and began a growing rampage in the woods between Weirwater and Karov.

The last assignment.o: In Spring 388YE the ageing prognosticator Mladen Escovitch reviewed, at the Imperial Master of Works' instruction, three expired opportunities to fortify Feroz, Morrow and Necropolis. He found two still viable and drew up two new alternative plans for the third.

The last leg.o: The Great Race sponsored by the Summer eternal Rhianos ended in Summer 387YE, with the captains who stayed Straight on for Glory claiming the winner's laurels and every fleet that completed the race receiving a permanent touch of Summer magic. Fleets that took no part each found a cold black pearl that the eternal is eager to buy back and destroy.

The lights of Temeschwar.o: In Autumn 383YE Temeschwar stirred with three opportunities: a guild-backed bid for the League to acquire the Fortress of Salt as a national Bourse seat, a push to raise an inspirational memorial to Boyar Ratibor, and growing interest in the strange ruins of Mellfort.

The little things.o: In Autumn 388YE the Thule of Otkodov remained at peace with the Empire. Through their ambassador Runa they proposed coordinating magic on shared territories, gave notice of a planned Summer enchantment on Ossium, ended military cooperation in Ulnak after taking Bonewall from the Druj, and offered payment for Imperial help against the Mirk Lizards.

The lives you love to lead.o: In Autumn 382YE the militia and magistrates were slowly winning the war on the outlawed drug bite, which was fuelling bravo violence across the League. A movement arose to return Empress Giselle's remains to Sarvos, Holberg completed its great new walls, and the Ilotari of Asavea offered leomarids to the Imperial Menagerie.

The long bench.o: At the Autumn Equinox of 384YE a host of visitors announced plans to come to Anvil, among them Sarcophan curse-sellers, Barien's heralds, a Varushkan seer, concerned priests, Marracossan exiles, Asavean 'priests', Tamazi orcs and Jarmish envoys. Sentinel Gate conjunctions to troubled Ketsov in Karsk and Calvos in Madruga were also identified.

The long march.o: In Spring 383YE the Highborn grey pilgrimage took to the trods in growing numbers, shaped by three Winter Solstice mandates of the Highborn National Assembly. The pilgrims set out to preach against idolatry and false virtues, convert visiting foreigners and question the faith of every human nation.

The long road.o: After a year in which a celestial conjunction blocked the ritual Challenge the Iron Duke, the heralds of Barien announced that the eternal would now set his own challenges, offering two for the Winter Solstice 386YE: a naval contest against a Summer sea beast and a mock battle against Jotun champions.

The mathematics of tears.o: After the Winter Solstice the Sarcophan Delves outlawed the slave trade, and several Sarcophan families and guilds put trade proposals to the Empire, including warehouses, docks, a bulk white granite sale and enclaves at Sarvos and Isember.

The matter will be done.o: In Spring 388YE the manticore styling itself Earl of the Groves challenged for the crown of Dawn, and Emperor Vesna answered by challenging for the Rose Throne herself. The matter was settled by grand tourney at Anvil, where Vesna's forces won overwhelmingly, Vesna was crowned Monarch of Dawn and the manticore was killed.

The money goes round.o: Merchant Prince Fransesca di Matos, with the Harlequin's backing, launched a year-long competition from Winter 384YE to find which of the League's four great cities invests the most wains in commissions and resources. The enthusiasm made business upgrades cheaper and revived several lapsed commission opportunities.

The moth for the star.o: Around the Autumn Equinox 387YE the stars grew turbulent: astronomancy became harder to practise and more prone to tulpa influence, the Claw's blood-empowered magic spread to the empower spell despite a Conclave interdiction, and a new grand conjunction of the Great Wyrm and the Drowned Shepherd began unravelling personal-curse arcane projections. Fresh 'night stars' were also seen under the Penumbral Veil.

The mother of morality.o: After the Wintermark and Freeborn assemblies, and narrowly the League's, condemned the cruelty of the Varushkan Iron Helms, the Synod was offered mandates to reshape how Imperial armies fight. Wintermark chose to fight the Jotun as heroes rather than butchers, and the Freeborn permanently turned the Red Wind Corsairs towards ransoming their foes.

The mystic, the willful.o: In Winter 382YE a round of magical effects touched the Empire and its neighbours: star-shrouds and Penumbral Veils persisted, magical citadels were raised, giant winter wolves appeared in Morrow, and Urizen magic sped castle-building and repairs. Several eternals also sent messages and offers, among them Kaela, Eleonaris, Sadogua, Callidus, Barien, Kimus and Jaheris.

The only reason that I sing.o: After the Dawnish troubadours named Summer champions for all seven virtues, plus champions of the Way, Love and Glory, Dawn had an opportunity to make Love and Glory permanent champion titles. Meanwhile the Senate's new Champion of Courage, keeper of the shield Torchbrand, stirred interest in recovering the six other lost Pilgrim's Shields.

The other empress.o: After the Grendel raided Sarvos, Highborn Unconquered rescued the remains of Empress Giselle from her tomb, setting off a dispute between Highguard and the League over where she should be re-interred. The Senate issued no ruling at the Summer Solstice, but by Spring 381YE she had been laid to rest in a new tomb, Virtue's Respite, in Temeschwar.

The parents of security.o: After the Grendel sack of Sarvos, the League was offered three opportunities: commissioning a Naval Arsenal, building a great chain fortification, and turning citizens against the Varushkan Iron Helms through a Synod mandate. Meanwhile most orcs freed from Jarm left the College of the Liberated for Skarsind. Neither the Senate nor the League Assembly acted on any of the opportunities that Autumn.

The path that winds.o: In Winter 382YE a curse of blight struck Urizen, and several opportunities to aid the beleaguered nation were raised: a rescue raid into Druj-held Zenith, a mithril Block to shield Spiral's spires, a ritual to collapse Morrow's passes, and messages of hope for Urizen and Dawn. The Senate commissioned the Block, but none of the other rituals were cast.

The place you called home.o: After the Empire refused to cede them a region of their own, the Great Forest Orcs who fled the Druj settled as guests in Therunin, centred on the Lower Tarn Valley, and disbanded their army. Several opportunities to aid them followed, and the Senate, Synod and Conclave took up most of them.

The play that came to Apulian.o: In Spring 387YE strange Night-tinged dramaturgical phenomena swept the city of Apulian, prompting League and Urizen magicians to propose an Academy or University of Dramaturgical Arts there. Meanwhile Sung's herald, the Spiral Dancer, grew increasingly agitated and renewed its urgent request for a fane in the city.

The poisoned air.o: In Spring 388YE, at the Urizen National Assembly's request, Urizeni seers used divination to locate the keystone miasma pillars of the newly conquered Sarangrave, at the cost of seers lost to the Druj. Their findings opened several conjunctions through which Imperial heroes could destroy the pillars.

The power behind our moves.o: Nearly 200 fleets and almost 100 military units evacuated the Freeborn from Grendel-held Feroz in a complete success, leaving only a handful of families behind. Governor Rahab retaliated, and the evacuees' resettlement in Madruga and Segura opened new opportunities there.

The prettiest star.o: A roundup of eternal activity at the Summer Solstice 387YE, covering bargains, challenges, offers and threats from eternals of all six realms. It included Volstann's terms on ceding regions, Meraud's support for Urizen, a herald battle in the Suaq Wastes and Ylenwe's restoration of scorched lands.

The price is great.o: The Civil Service's Winter 387YE diplomatic report on the Commonwealth announced that the Commonwealth embassy, the Diplomatenschloss in Necropolis, had been completed and garrisoned. It also set out options for a patrol on the Couros river, Commonwealth accusations of Imperial trade with Jarm, and a proposed exchange on love with Dawn.

The price of liberty.o: After the Liberty Pact was signed at the Winter Solstice, its trade sanctions on slaving nations cost the Imperial treasury a net 143 thrones and 4 crowns each season. A civil service appraisal led by Naomi of Virtue's Rest set out the losses and proposed ways to mitigate them.

The price of peace.o: In Summer 386YE the civil service set out the state of the Empire's foreign relations: the Thule refused to negotiate a renewed peace unless the Senate passed their exact wording renouncing six ceded regions, while the Grendel, the Iron Confederacy, Skoura and a Lasambrian Jotun delegation each made overtures of their own.

The price of wisdom.o: After Wisdom Assembly and sword-scholar challenges stopped several Autumn mandates taking hold, Synod mandates came to need a greater majority to be enacted. This Wind of Fortune set out competing responses for the General, Wisdom, Urizen, Brass Coast and other assemblies, and a Senate opportunity to fund fortified sword scholar temples in Morrow.

The prime colour of the world.o: At the Spring Equinox the Sherard Hunters of Wintermark wove the Hallow of the Green World across the Empire under the conjunction of the Fountain, unleashing a season of extraordinary fertility, extra Cerulean Mazzarine, rare Realmsroot blooms and strengthened Spring magic, but also hastening the spread of the Morass in Holberg.

The risk-all point.o: In Spring 383YE the Empire's foreign relations were reshaped by the Liberty Pact, signed by the Empire, the Sumaah Republic, the Commonwealth and Axos, and by trade sanctions on the slaving nations, which responded with tariffs and embargoes of their own.

The sack of Sarvos.o: In Spring 380YE the Grendel invaded the League city of Sarvos, conquering the island of Cigno and imposing draconian martial law while they systematically pillaged one of the richest cities in the Empire.

The same bed.o: In Summer 382YE the Brass Coast, despite invasions by the Grendel and Jotun, buzzed with talk of nightly fiery displays of Imperial victories over Madruga, an earthquake at Ghita's Veils in Segura, a League architect's proposal to fortify Siroc, and a Freeborn Assembly statement on charity.

The scars from tomorrow.o: In Autumn 382YE the Navarr weighed a Synod mandate to send guides to escort foreigners on the trods, the Wither the Seed curse began sending Liathaven's vallorn into a thirty-year slumber, and the vallorn of Brocéliande was deliberately roused to creep into Boar's Dell and Elerael.

The shadows fall behind you.o: After the Fist of the Mountains sacrificed itself to stop the Grendel destroying Elos with a weapon called Maelstrom, the Ambition Assembly sought true consecration of the restored Elos docks in Redoubt, where the army's last banner flies. Competing Synod mandates were drawn up, some also honouring the Grendel's own Ambition.

The shape of things to come.o: In Spring 387YE the Parador of the Silver Tears, funded by the Conclave, drew up plans for the Well of Life, a grand lodge for the Silver Chalice at the restored Jayyani Caravanserai near Quzar in Lightsea, Madruga. The page also set out how further grand lodges for other Conclave orders could be planned.

The silent page.o: Imperial armies invading the Barrens, led by the Valiant Pegasus and Gryphon's Pride, held back from full conquest to reach out to the territory's embittered inhabitants. This created Synod mandate opportunities to approach one of six local factions, and competing mandates either embracing or condemning the cry "Death to the Druj".

The stars aren't right.o: In Winter 379YE a round-up of magical phenomena across the Empire reported protective night enchantments on the western marshes, continuing shrouds over the northern Bay of Catazar, Madruga, Zenith and Tassato, and the Thule permanently binding the Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae into the Silver Peaks with ilium.

The sweetest of songs.o: After the Summer Solstice 384YE, the Empire joined its Liberty Pact allies in free trade and an embargo on Jarm, and Jarm cut all ties in return. The Thule and the Faraden both abolished slavery and asked for sanctions to be lifted, while Sarcophan, Bregasland, Iron Confederacy, Grendel and Asavean affairs also moved on.

The tale that speaks to your heart.o: The Sumaah Republic sent its seasonal diplomatic news to the Empire. It thanked Imperial fleets for their help against the Asavean Archipelago, rewarded rituals and rescuers, and reported that its Houses of Virtue had begun recognising Alberto Acciai, rather than Amika, as an exemplar of Courage.

The thing with feathers.o: In Winter 387YE a host of eternals reached out to the Empire with offers, challenges and warnings. Among them were Agramant tempting the beleaguered Navarr of Therunin, Cathan Canae's test at Hope's Rest nearing completion, Irra Harah's watchtowers for Nesustak Forest and Estavus's finalised Office of Fire and Stone in Zenith.

The three pillars.o: In Spring 386YE, rebel Urizeni spires held parts of Spiral after the territory was allocated to the League. The Constitutional Court offered two constitutional motions to make the Warmage an Urizeni national position, which would end Tiborion's rebellion in Ankra. Grendel mercenaries also threatened Spiral.

The troubled words.o: After a new sword academy was commissioned in Holberg and Urizeni sword scholars agreed to teach there, the League Assembly was given the opportunity to decide whether Holberg's bravos should embrace or reject the sword scholars' philosophy, which echoes the executed local preacher Alexander von Holberg.

The truth but tell it slant.o: Professor Immanuel Gelberg's Commonwealth appraisers, working under the Beurteilung at the Printers' Guild's request, proposed three commissions to expand printing in Tassato, plus a student's subsidiary plan to revive the struggling Moor's Mill guild.

The tune without the words.o: A Winter 387YE roundup of strange magical events across the Empire. Five new rituals entered Urizen lore, cursed storms struck Madruga, Feroz and Sarvos, coral husks massed around the Gullet, and a Navarri arcane projection spread a song through the trods.

The twentieth empress.o: The Senate appointed Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League as the twentieth Empress, elected during the Spring Equinox 380YE, with her formal coronation set for the Summer Solstice.

The two of us.o: Lady Nimue de Moraine's scheme for the enchantresses of Dawn to win five Summer eternals as patrons of the Eastern Sky moved forward, with the eternals setting out their terms and two alternative approaches, a Night-magic trick on Eleonaris' statue and a turn to the Winter realm, put forward.

The virtue of sharing.o: Dawnish and Highborn assemblies sought to learn from each other in supporting the reconquest of Dark Ranging from the vallorn, while a demand for a public inquisition into the Druj alliance in Brocéliande ended with Galene Netherwatch vindicating Harwyn Eternal. Ranae de Rondell later enacted a mandate rewarding Dawnish knights who fight in Dark Ranging.

The war makers.o: The third Navarr army, raised in Hercynia around the artisans and runesmiths of Treji, finished mustering, and its raising senator was asked to choose its name and quality. It was named the Star Forged and given the Resourceful quality.

The war of thorns and flowers.o: In Winter 386YE several Imperial nations prepared for the war against the vallorn. Highguard recalled its grey pilgrims to raise a fourth army, the League proposed road tolls to fund the war, and Varushka looked to dark powers. Dawn, Urizen and Wintermark held back.

The warmth of an invisible light.o: Several hundred Imperial heroes from Urizen, Dawn, Highguard, the League, Wintermark and Varushka raided Druj-occupied Zenith and freed more than half of its remaining enslaved inhabitants. The Urizen National Assembly then endorsed a mandate urging the rescued refugees to resettle in Morrow and Redoubt.

The way home.o: Following Winifred Blackhawk's Winter Solstice judgement on the importance of the trods and wayhouses, the civil servant Eilian Sweetwater proposed that the Navarr build large wayhouses outside their own territories, presented alongside three specific wayhouse opportunities.

The way that the sunshine gleams.o: After a year closed to the Empire following an attack on its archives, the eternal Phaleron announced that it would reopen its doors, offering a new ritual, a proposed Imperial title, protection for the Anvil Library and sanctuary for the Urizeni of Morrow and Zenith.

The whole world.o: In Spring 382YE this diplomatic Wind of Fortune updated the Empire's foreign relations. It reported a violent coup in Rigia, a Sumaah peace delegation coming to Anvil and an Axou proposal to end slavery, and set out Sarcophan, Axou and Jarmish offers to help fortify Cargo against a possible Druj advance.

The widening gyre.o: Dogri Thulebane, the rebellious Wintermark thane holding Crows Ridge in Skarsind against the Senate's will, killed Thule traders and turned away an Imperial Orc magistrate, and was rumoured to be gathering warriors for a raid into Thule lands. The Wind laid out options to support the raid, prevent it, or betray him to the Thule.

The wild wind rises.o: In Autumn 386YE the Tusks, Green Shield, Bloodcloaks and Quiet Step marched to drive the Jotun from the Mournwold. More than sixty thousand Jotun and Summer allies overwhelmed them, taking Southmoor, Greensward, Ore Hills and Chalkdowns, and the Mournwold ceased to be Imperial territory.

The winds of fashion.o: In the wake of Skathe's mirror-shattering curse, Sarvos weathered arson and a major waterfront fire as the House Bourné School of Couture was completed, opening the way for the League to remake Sarvos as the City of Masks. After the Winter Solstice 383YE, Aureliana di Sarvos enacted the mandate that formally renewed it as such.

The wolves tempt you.o: In Autumn 388YE Emperor Vesna addressed the whole Empire, honouring the fallen Iron Helms and urging every citizen not to be tempted from the path by the Wolves but to remember who has fought and died for them.

The worth of a life.o: In Winter 379YE many experienced Imperial Orc bonesetters settled in newly held Skarsind, presenting three Senate-backed opportunities: a ministry recruiting human miners, a memorial great work of herb gardens, and a network of northern trade ministries. The Senate commissioned the miners' ministry in Gulhule, began trading posts in Torfast and the Glen of Shadows, and the Fellowship of the Red Blade's great work was completed.

Theory of the crows.o: In Winter 386YE the Sarcophan Delves, angered that Asavean bounties were harming their shipping, proposed a Free Seas Pact with the Empire to outlaw piracy. Their ambassador, Bedelaar Huisbaas Annike, also set out a range of trade offers, meetings and diplomatic replies.

There is hope.o: The magical chaos that had gripped the Empire's astronomancy since the Winter Solstice abated, leaving behind a nineteenth constellation, the Beacon, whose law is 'there is hope'. Embodied tulpas vanished, and the Imperial regio at Anvil remained partly altered for one final season.

There is thunder.o: The Sumaah House of the People planned a surprise raid on Chalonsio, the heart of the Asavean slave trade, and invited the Empire to join it alongside the Commonwealth. Imperial captains could only take part if the Senate legalised the action or declared war on Asavea.

They bit the cats.o: In spring 386YE Temeschwar suffered a plague of unnaturally bold and vicious rats, culminating in the gruesome killing of an apothecary beside a bloody message about the volodny Shadowsmith. Meanwhile a mysterious sickness struck workers at Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Things go awry.o: In Spring 388YE magical chaos tied to an unprecedented astronomantic conjunction kept the Imperial regio unable to enhance ritual lore and caused territory-scale magic across the Empire to have unpredictable side effects. It also opened several opportunities and dangers, from Feroz to Redoubt, Mitwold, Miekarova and Sermersuaq.

Things that burn.o: In Winter 385YE, armies of scions of the eternal Cold Sun, tens of thousands strong after emerging from regio across the Empire, ravaged Wintermark, Varushka, Navarr, the Brass Coast, the Marches and Highguard, while Imperial armies, warbands and enchantments fought back.

Think of the children.o: After the Assembly of Prosperity upheld Cesare Enzo di Trivento's call for a great orphanage for the Mournwold's orphans, Marcher friars instead proposed the Sarcombe Register, a central record of households to help place orphans with relatives and foster families. Separately, the Holberg architect Frederick di Sarvos challenged the Cardinal of Ambition to pass a 'Statement of Endeavour'.

This is the end.o: In Summer 388YE the songbirds of Sung drove the Whisper Gallery's cats out of Apulian, and Sofonisba Amilcara became the Map to the City Below after military units uncovered and destroyed a hidden Whisper Gallery lair. Sadogua and the Azoth also proposed edifices of their own in the city.

This land is your land.o: After the Jotun were driven from the Mournwold, the Empire's response to the demands carried to Anvil by Mel Greenhill, Long Tom and Edda Counter calmed talk of rebellion there. Further opportunities remained to win the territory's lasting loyalty.

This little light of mine.o: In Summer 384YE nearly forty thousand Imperial soldiers from five nations fought an equal Druj host in Zenith and narrowly pushed the orcs back in Clypion, leaving the Empire nine-tenths of the way to a beachhead. The page also set out a Summer Solstice battle to kill Karvor Eyepeel and several conjunctions.

This might be your battle.o: Spurred by a Freeborn statement of principle calling for privateers to strike Grendel slavers, an opportunity arose in Autumn 382YE for Imperial fleets and military units to raid the Broken Shore, free slaves and disrupt the Grendel. It was available only for the Autumn Equinox and the season that followed.

This old house.o: In Autumn 388YE the Prosperity Assembly's work to rebuild Feroz prompted two proposed Synod mandates. One would lift the abandoned quality from Oranseri and Afarjasse, and the other, put forward by a Freeborn architect, would raise wages for labourers and architects across the Empire.

Thorn and bone.o: In Summer 388YE the Black Thorns, Boyar's Hasta and Granite Pillar, fighting alongside the Nesustak rebels, drove the vallorn of Bendol back out of Nesustak Forest. In Turan Flats the Citadel Guard and Golden Axe defeated an invasion by the Druj Hidden Snake and Poison Crane, who were then trapped in Sarangrave when their own kin in the Salt Flats of Sanath refused to let them return.

Those memories of you.o: An Autumn 388YE Wind of Fortune updated Imperial relations with the Sarcophan Delves and the Citadels of Axos. It covered Sarcophan unhappiness at new mercantilist tariffs, a herb opportunity in Hahnmark and a price for keeping the Jakhalsmarkt open, alongside Axou settlement of Thornfen and their frustrations over Sarangrave.

Those that break a thing.o: In Autumn 387YE the Children of Wrecks attacked Trivento in Sarvos for a second time with a larger armada. They were driven off by the Great Chain, the garrison of Our Lady of Pride and the Red Wind Corsairs, who took heavy losses but completed their transformation into an Imperial navy.

Those who worship.o: In Winter 380YE the Asavean temple of Balo and the Black Bull in the port of Oran neared completion and was expected to open to Asavean sailors by the Spring Equinox 381YE. Its completion would allow a reciprocal temple of the Way to be built in Nemoria, the Asavean capital.

Thoughts are free (Trade Winds).o: In Autumn 380YE, trade captains brought news of how foreign powers reacted to the Senate's statement denouncing slavery and to other Imperial affairs. The Commonwealth eased its trade restrictions, Asavea grew displeased, Jarm shrugged, the Sumaah stayed hostile, and Axos opened its ports to Imperial trade.

Thousands or more.o: After Ossium's conquest, the civil service surveyed the territory's wealth and catalogued five captured Druj structures that could become Imperial titles, along with further development opportunities. The Senate then decided that all five titles would be appointed by unanimous decision of the Varushkan senators.

Threats that are to come.o: Professor Immanuel Gelberg's Commonwealth appraisers, Die Beurteilung, assessed ways to secure Holberg's food and water against future sieges or a flood of refugees. They proposed three opportunities: deep wells with seven grain stores, draining marshland with the Seven Dykes, and persuading the Sand Fishers to farm the drained land.

Three and three.o: In the run-up to the Summer Solstice of 385YE, six eternals answered plenipotentiary messages sent by the Empire's archmages at the Spring Equinox. Three agreed to formal parleys, while the others declined or made other arrangements.

Three celebrations and a funeral.o: Fire gutted the Basilica of the Little Mother in Bastion, killing Prelate Marianne di Sarvos as she rescued children. At the same time the Synod was offered chances to honour Zemress, Adelmar the Lion and Zoria. The basilica's repair was later commissioned, and the General Assembly backed consecrating the Academy of Arms in Redoubt.

Three keys.o: After the Empire accepted three boons from Zakalwe, General of Day, at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, his heralds proposed ways to hone two Imperial armies and strengthen fortifications across the Empire. Zakalwe also rewarded the Conclave's interdiction of savagery-inducing magic with an extra ritual boon.

Three soldiers.o: Koboldi lent by the eternal Adamant completed the Three Watchers, three colossal statues of Highborn soldiers carved into the mountains to guard the High Pass between Morrow and Zenith, with a shrine consecrated with an aura of Loyalty at their base. The monument now strengthens Highborn and Urizen armies fighting over the pass, draws Highborn pilgrims, and lets the Highborn assembly choose a new permanent strategy for its armies.

Thresher's summer.o: Following mandates from the Urizen and Marcher national assemblies, hundreds of Urizeni mages, sentinels and scholars helped bring in the Marcher harvest while scores of Marcher friars and monks shared their Virtue in Urizen, easing the rift between the two nations. The exchange inspired two commissions, a Landskeeper's Study and a Monastery of the Four Winds, both of which the Senate chose to build.

Thrones and principalities.o: The civil service's Summer 386YE report on the Principalities of Jarm found relations still bitter under a mutual trade embargo. It also set out a Jarmish offer to trade the relic shield Measure for the ritual Brotherhood of Tian and a request from the merchant Circle of Six to buy goods through the Artisans Guild.

Through my sails.o: The Summer 383YE Wind of Fortune set out the state of the Empire's relations with its human neighbours: Suranni executions of Imperial citizens and a new Iron Confederacy envoy, mob damage to the Imperial temple in Nemoria, fresh Sarcophan enclave offers, and Sumaah plans for talks on the Way. The Synod then enacted a mandate sending Tarquinius Ankarien to urge trade with Axos.

Throw back the echoes.o: After the General Assembly rebuked any campaign of conquest in the Barrens, Dawn was presented with Synod mandates to answer the rebuke and with offers of aid from the eternals Jaheris, Janon and Tharim to press its ancient claim. A conjunction also gave House Aurelius a chance to summon Sorin's wolves against the Druj.

Time and time again.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest delivered the Senate's requested appraisal of how to restore Kahraman's roads and bridges, which the Jotun had sabotaged in 384YE. She set out the economic damage, short-term and long-term remedies, and foreign offers of help, while two Jotun bands threatened traders in the Jade Range.

Tired of sleeping.o: Answering the Imperial Orc call, nearly 120 Imperial fleet captains sailed to Axos and brought away every orc who wished to leave, along with a few human former slaves. The freed orcs, who call themselves the Tamazi, began settling in Skarsind, while the angered Axou imposed a chilly reception on Imperial trade.

To curb those raging appetites.o: After the Senate ceded Feroz to the Grendel by treaty, the Freeborn faced harsh orc rule under Governor Lord Rahab, and the Brass Coast assembly weighed three competing mandates on how the Freeborn of Feroz should respond. Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra enacted the mandate urging them to abandon the territory.

To fight aloud.o: In Winter 387YE, after Senate, Conclave and Synod alike condemned them, Urizeni captains crushed the Disciples of Sulemaine across Redoubt, Morrow and Zenith, capturing their leader Severus of the Blinding Sun and scattering the survivors.

To hold death's hand in mine.o: After the Imperial armies withdrew west, the Druj overran Therunin in the winter of 386YE, conquering all but the vallorn regions while the Navarr assemblies urged the people to flee. Only Peakedge Stead held, behind a temporary hedge raised by Ossegrahn, and the Tainted Basilisk roused the vallorn of Tharunind.

To loose the fateful lightning.o: In Spring 383YE Grendel pirates kept raiding Imperial shipping on the Bay of Catazar. Imperial fleet captains, coordinated by the Freeborn corsairs and the Imperial Fleet Master, were offered a one-season chance to mount a bay-wide attack, Dominate the Bay, against the overconfident pirates.

To ride the earth.o: In Summer 384YE the Imperial campaign to free Zenith from the Druj gained momentum, and Urizen's Loyalty-driven support for the Citadel Guard secured its supply for a year. Two Synod opportunities followed: a General Assembly mandate to aid armies in Zenith, and a Urizen Assembly mandate that could disband the Citadel Guard.

To ruin.o: In Autumn 387YE a Grendel armada of four navies and five Asavean battleships seized Elos and all of Naris in Redoubt. The Fist of the Mountains was destroyed stopping them from using a stolen tempest jade sphere to devastate the harbour.

To see what you sell.o: In Spring 384YE several Prosperity-driven opportunities emerged. Redoubt was offered a chance to restore the old port of Elos, the Sand Fisher orcs took up Imperial offers of learning and planned to repay the Empire, and the Freeborn began debating a new festival of Prosperity as a mysterious tomb of a forgotten exemplar was found in Gambit.

To sleep in Kallavesa.o: Highborn and Winterfolk removed Empress Britta's relics from her shrine in Necropolis and sank them in the lake at Sovvengard in Kallavesa, reuniting them with her body according to Wintermark custom. The Senate then commissioned a major shrine to her and a pilgrims' trail across the marshes.

To the last syllable.o: After Urizen magicians cast Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths, Day regio across the Empire flourished, and the eternal Cold Sun sent its blue-clad heralds through them to attack Imperial landmarks and people. By the Autumn Equinox these raids had grown into eight armies of roughly three thousand each, set on destroying the Empire.

Tomb of the Courageous.o: After the Courage Assembly resolved in Spring 388YE to consecrate the tomb of Emperor Ahraz, the General Assembly of the Synod was offered two competing mandates to frame the consecration. Each could strengthen either the Imperial Orcs or the Brass Coast, and the Senate was offered a chance to raise a statue to Ahraz in Kahraman.

Too much of nothing.o: After the fall of Drycastle to the Druj, several minor characters were expected at Anvil in Summer 381YE to sell rare goods. These included Earl Hugo of House Renard with the last Barrenberry seeds, and a Dawnish seneschal with a lost senator's writings.

Tooth by tooth.o: Following a Pride Assembly judgement by Ubarius of Tropaion Citadel, urging priests to convert foreigners living in the Empire without the Way, the Cardinal of Pride gained the chance to direct missionary work each summit until Winter 385YE. Priests were ultimately sent to the Faraden, the hylje and the Great Forest Orcs.

Top and Bottom, Up and Down.o: After the Conclave asked the Turning Mirror how the harm from Empire-wide Omnihedron rituals might be fixed, Sinokenon's heralds roamed the Empire offering mostly self-serving advice, along with two practical opportunities. Heralds of the Night, Winter and Spring realms also joined the debate with opposing views.

Touch the night.o: After a night coven cast Wondrous Forests of the Night at the Spring Equinox, every forest in the Empire yielded extra bounty, naga felt a powerful pull of their blood, and lingering ripples altered several rituals for the Summer Solstice. Several Night eternals also offered gifts to the Empire.

Tourney of the Damned.o: The Deadwood Knight, an unliving lieutenant of the Howling Queen also called the Schlacta of Rot, finished gathering an army of the dead equivalent to a campaign army, poised to attack Weirwater or Karov after the Autumn Equinox. A last chance arose to challenge him to a grand melee and end his rampage.

Tourney of two cities.o: The rival military academies of Tassato, the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy and the Five Cities Military Academy, asked the Anvil Academy to arrange a sponsored fighting tourney at the Anvil arena. The first Twin Cities Tourney was announced as a way to find young recruits.

Towards a common good.o: Die Beurteilung, led by Professor Immanuel Gelberg, appraised how Highguard and the Commonwealth could forge stronger ties, on behalf of Solomon of the Shattered Tower. It identified three avenues: military doctrine, a witch-hunters' academy and legalising the preaching of the Common Good.

Towers and crows.o: In Summer 386YE the Sarcophan Delves, through ambassador Bedelaar Huisbaas Annike, offered to open negotiations to buy Imperial bourse materials, including a higher price for weirwood they would sell on to the Grendel. They also complained about storms in the Bay of Catazar and Sarvos, withdrew from intelligence sharing, and refused to help with the Elakar or the Book of Silence.

Towers behind the moon.o: A Wind of Fortune for Winter 383YE reported the lingering effects of magic cast at the Autumn Equinox, from shrouds, a curse and twelve magical fortifications, and relayed news from the eternals. Tharim announced a new Keeper of Tharim's Throne, and the Druj freed a hundred slaves at Parel.

Towers of the moon.o: In Autumn 388YE the eternal Sadogua, Brother of Wizards, roused himself to catch up on obligations to his Imperial friends, offering a string of boons and opportunities across Wintermark, the Marches, the Brass Coast and Varushka.

Towers of the sun.o: In Autumn 388YE heralds of Meraud, the Summer Enchanter, brought the Empire plans for Summer wizard towers with a contest for the grandest, a proposal that he appoint the Churnspire Adjutor, and a request to replace From the Mouth of Babes with a new ritual. He also promised replies to last season's missives.

Trade all my tomorrows.o: In Autumn 382YE a new road from Delev to Kalpaheim was quietly linking Varushkan miners with the Steinr artisans of Hahnmark, and Wintermark was offered the chance to join the northern trade network by building a Trade Hall in Kalpaheim. Several traders also announced visits to Anvil with unusual goods and proposals.

Trade winds.o: Imperial ship captains found their dealings with foreign powers soured in Summer 379YE: Jarm's northern and southern ports turned cold after the Empire's embassy went to eastern Rigia, the Commonwealth imposed tariffs, Sumaah met traders with fury, and Grendel warships began hunting Imperial raiders in the Bay of Catazar.

Tread of dust and darkness.o: In Summer 386YE, following the Empire's decisive Spring victory over the Dry Patricians, the Blight in Madruga's former Great Grasses lay quiescent but undefeated. Several opportunities arose to end it for good, including a Sentinel Gate conjunction to its very heart.

Troop of echoes.o: In Autumn 387YE the Citadels of Axos, under their new ambassador Ilarch Skopos of Solokha, announced a formal delegation to Anvil and called a Liberty Pact meeting for the Winter Solstice. They also raised concerns about espionage in Maykop and proposed that Axou officers study at the Five Cities Military Academy.

Trove remade.o: The trove of mage weapons and armour found beneath the ruins of the Unmade Spire in Redoubt was imbued with ilium and used to equip the Citadel Guard. This gave the army a new Cyclic Resonance quality tied to the six realms of magic.

True faith.o: After the Lepidean Librarian published research showing that Vardas, a paragon of Vigilance, never existed and was the invention of a League fraudster, a crisis of faith spread across the Empire. The General Assembly ultimately revoked its recognition of Vardas, heading off the crisis but inviting hard questions about the other paragons.

Turbulence.o: In Autumn 380YE an unnatural cycle of dead calm by day and violent storms by night gripped the Semmerlak, while monstrous creatures called Semmerfolk, kalpie or rusalka began attacking people on and near the lake.

Twelfth of never.o: In Autumn 388YE a small Druj delegation under a flag of truce brought the Empire an offer of conditional surrender from the Congress of Buruk Tepel: an Imperial withdrawal from the Salt Flats of Sanath and the Forest of Ulnak in exchange for a truce and, eventually, a Black Lotus plant.

Two for joy.o: After the Senate approved the creation of the Magpies, a new Imperial sodality devoted to recovering lost artefacts, the civil service found it had failed to obtain Throne ratification, leaving the sodality in suspension. Constitutional questions over historical research and salvage rights were raised, and several groups offered patronage in exchange for changes to its manifesto.

Two minutes.o: In the wake of the Spring Equinox 385YE, several Conclave declarations took effect. A Celestial Arch delegation won goodwill with Faraden magician families, the Quiet Hall was endowed on the Custodian of the Lost, the bleeding ice rock in Tanikipari was destroyed, and the Suranni wizards began settling in the Empire.

Two silhouettes.o: At the Winter Solstice 384YE, prognosticators identified two Saturday-morning opportunities for Imperial heroes to strike into the Barrens, with the Military Council to choose between them, alongside three smaller conjunctions against Druj forces.

Two steps on the water.o: Two groups of Asavean refugees sought to settle in the Empire in Summer 384YE: the Free Folk, former slaves living in Astolat whose unorthodox veneration of 'Divines' drew accusations of idolatry, and the Marracossans, exiled rebels at Trajadoz in Madruga who asked the Senate to cede the town to them.

Two suns in the sunset.o: In Spring 387YE the Loyalty Assembly's call to overthrow the Asavean Plenum identified three possible rebel groups, while efforts to anchor the Way in Asavea stalled amid public weariness. Nearly a hundred Imperial fleets joined the Frieøyer to defend the Sumaah city of Zemeh and forced five Asavean navies to retreat.

Unable to see.o: After the Imperial Synod condemned Yael of Highguard, who claimed to be the First Empress reborn, for heresy and she was executed, Highguard mourned her. The nation stood doctrinally at odds with the rest of the Empire until the Highborn Assembly backed a mandate to return its people to orthodoxy.

Under eastern skies.o: In Winter 386YE an Imperial push to drive the Druj from Therunin walked into a Spring-warded trap in Eastring. Isaella's Dance and the Iron Helms were destroyed covering the escape of the surviving armies into the Barrens, and the Druj retook Eastring.

Under heaven.o: In Summer 384YE a large Imperial raid led by Orrick of House Bolholt struck Skallahn from Odd's End and Westerhal, looting mines, forges and quarries while Imperial fleets dominated the Gullet, raided Kierheim's docks and wrecked the Kongegőr land bridge.

Under the firelight.o: In Spring 386YE the Military Council was presented with three Jotun-related opportunities: a battle at Wyndyn Path in Liathaven, where Autumn heralds of Estavus were clearing forest for Jotun settlement; a Jotun raid on the sacred marshes of Hvalgrunn in Kallavesa; and a warband raid on the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq.

Under the red sky.o: In Summer 381YE, five eternals answered the Spring Equinox plenipotentiary missives from the Imperial archmages with open, formal responses, arranging parleys, meetings and herald visits for the Summer Solstice. The most prominent was the Thrice-cursed Court, which agreed to a full formal parley.

Underwater sunshine.o: In Spring 385YE the new Varushkan port of Kostjyas Respite opened on the Semmerlak, boosting taxation in the surrounding Imperial territories except Holberg. At the same time the lake sovereign Dho'uala stirred, and people and cargo began vanishing from the lake.

United in law.o: Imperatrix Lisabetta von Holberg addressed the whole Empire, urging citizens to honour their oath to support Imperial law, announcing her intention to seek a spouse through the House of Seven Mirrors, and granting an Imperial Charter to the market town of Sarcombe in Southmoor.

Unleashing the storm.o: After the sack of Dubhtraig, Queen Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea, steered the Empire towards a raid on Beoraidh in Grendel-held Mareave, where a great coliseum serves as a slave market and army training ground. During the Winter Solstice the Quartermaster General declared that fleets and military units joining the raid would share in the Imperial Guerdon.

Unlock thy hidden gate.o: In Spring 387YE four Imperial armies marched from Lustri into the Sarangrave, defeated the Druj at the Battle of Tabun and came a little over halfway to securing a beachhead in the Bloodwater Marsh. The advance also revealed the Mirelith, a Terunael ward holding back the Bendol vallorn, which created a battle opportunity.

Unmade trove.o: Torchbearer Drusa of Mute Spire found a trove of non-magical battle mage's staffs and armour in a vaulted chamber beneath the ruins of the Unmade Spire in Redoubt. Urizen was offered a choice over how to use it.

Unspoken words.o: Tensions persisted in the Barrens in Autumn 386YE as the Imperial Orcs and Dawnish Assembly reached out to the Rahvin ahead of winter, Dawn's generals were challenged to swear an oath protecting the Barrens orcs, and strange new trods were found through the mysterious Untrod Groves. After negotiations between Senator Aramis du Froste and the Karass, Dawnish knights were able to explore the Groves for their wealth.

Unwelcome guest.o: In Summer 379YE the Seventh Wave, under General Cuth, located and destroyed a vallorn infestation growing in a Spring regio in Casinea. The army suffered over ninety casualties, and two strange pods found at the site were sent to Anvil for the Conclave.

Up on Whittle Hill.o: Imperial patrols probing into Freemoor in the Jotun-held Mournwold made contact with Whittle, a Marcher village that had held out against the Jotun for thirty years, cut off from the rest of the Empire.

Upgrade Grimhold.o: In Summer 387YE the Master of the Koboldi, Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, announced a commission to upgrade the Grimhold, a fortification in Perumaki, Miekarova.

Upgrade Palace of Apulian.o: In Summer 388YE the Imperial Master of Works, Ehud, announced the start of work to upgrade the Palace of Apulian fortification in Apulus, Spiral, which would be renamed the Palace of Mists once complete.

Upgrade the Red Wind Corsairs.o: The Senate passed a motion proposed by Chiara Zayden Riqueza, Citizens' Voice, to upgrade the Red Wind Corsairs with the Forayers quality, letting the army convert between an army and a navy. The upgrade followed the An angry blade Wind of Fortune and was completed.

Upon a midnight dreary.o: In Autumn 387YE eternals of every realm approached the Empire with offers, warnings and consequences. Irra Harah backed slave rebels in Sarangrave's Nesustak Forest, Ossegrahn turned away after Peakedge Stead fell, Surut's knights guarded Necropolis, and Tharim's knights scoured Upwold.

Urizeni Experiment.o: After the Urizen National Assembly called on the Stargazers to study the Sarangrave's vallorn, they identified conjunctions to place permanent wards in Bloodwater Marsh and to connect the Bendol vallorn heart to the trods. Alongside this, the Nesustak Forest rebels postponed their delegation to Anvil, and a Severed Hornet orc revealed the mithril-rich caves of the Hungry Earth in the Whisperwood.

Value beneath the mountain.o: Heralds of the Argent Sword, sent by General Clytemnestra to explore the crevasse beneath the newly raised Kespoena's Reach in Occursion, discovered a deep vein of mithril, along with caverns haunted by hostile creatures. A new mithril bourse seat, Kespoena's Nadir, could now be commissioned.
