Various storms and saints.o: A seasonal roundup of magical happenings across the Empire in Autumn 385YE: the Unfettered Mind identified the eternals behind two citadel rituals, Sadogua moved the ruins of Damakhan's Forge to Zenith, Sanvar Isk opened the Loom of Spells in Tassato, and several eternals made offers. A Varushkan expedition also found Zoria's Cave claimed by a hungry darkness.

Vermin.o: In Winter 379YE the newly liberated League territory of Holberg faced the Druj occupation's aftermath: animated trees battering its walls, vermin overrunning the ruins of Holmauer, the Morass spreading north and poisonous briars in the northern forests. Meanwhile the Towerjacks army was re-formed and needed a general.

Victory and unity.o: In Autumn 386YE, Imperial relations with the Citadels of Axos stayed rocky as the demagogue Ilarch Kyther Deianeira rallied Axou to a populist call for unity. His rise was backed by Imperial liao and a letter from Emperor Vesna, while signs of foreign investment and a plan to reclaim haunted Solokha drew Imperial attention.

Viridian nemesis.o: In Summer 388YE, after the Navarr and Loyalty Assemblies sent their people to share their vallorn-fighting knowledge with the League and the League Assembly welcomed the aid, each League city drew up its own plan to prepare the Vallornguard for war against the Doom of Terunael.

Voice irresistable.o: In Spring 388YE the new Thule ambassador, Runa Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided, succeeded the late Rak. He proposed a private Summer Solstice meeting, renewed offers on ritual texts, weirwood and ward appraisals, and protested Imperial magic laid over Thule-held lands, while the Thule claimed victory in their first assault on the Forest of Ulnak.

Volumes of forgotten lore.o: An Autumn 387YE wind of fortune gathered a range of strange magical events across the Empire. These included a costly sky-vision of Empress Vesna over Casinea, an offer from the shadowy Blackdamp to Varushka, and Marcher gratitude after the Conclave kept Rivers Run Red interdicted.

Wages of sin.o: In autumn 382YE, as Asavea sought Imperial mercenaries to crush the revolt in Marracoss and Emphedor, the Imperial Temple in Nemoria and a young League bishop sought Synod guidance on how the Empire should respond. Three possible mandates were proposed, and the Senate was left weighing whether to close the Temple.

Waiting for the worms.o: In Spring 387YE the Sarcophan Delves reported that their proposed Free Seas Pact against piracy had foundered over conflicts with the Liberty Pact, and warned that Asavean privateering would push the prices of their goods up by as much as a fifth. The Wind also covered developments in Sarvos, Holberg, Wintermark and Highguard, and an offer to buy surplus wains if Imperial prices collapsed.

Wake up crying.o: Shortly before the Summer Solstice 384YE, a catastrophic flood tainted with Winter magic tore through the silver and ilium mine of Syrene's Wisdom in Casinea and down into the town of Syrene. It killed miners, ruined homes and fields, and left the mine's future production in doubt.

Walk on.o: Grey pilgrims from Highguard, walking the trods to weaken the vallorn, questioned people across the Empire about their faith, leaving many citizens doubting nation-specific beliefs and congregations thinner. The Synod was offered mandates to settle these questions, and the General Assembly enacted every one except Dawn's.

Walk with me.o: Emperor Vesna marked a year on the throne with an address to all Imperial citizens. The Throne urged every citizen to open their homes to the displaced people of Therunin and honoured the murdered senator Earl Aramis Du Froste.

War games.o: In Summer 388YE a summit brokered by Prospero to arrange a ceasefire between the Commonwealth and Jarm against Cold Sun collapsed into recriminations, after Imperial ambassadors had told both powers that the Empire knew who caused the Lantir incursion.

Ward Little Boyar's Welcome.o: In Spring 387YE the Senate passed a motion, proposed by Karov's senator and seconded by Volodmartz's, to ward the walls of the Little Boyar's Welcome, a fortification in Duzekani, against supernatural threats.

Warriors' Gate.o: Winterfolk scouts, a band of Navarr and Dawnish adventurers made the first successful foray into Tsirku in Summer 388YE, mapping the region now called Warriors' Gate. The Empire was offered ways to build on this, including a proposed citadel, a hunt against Agramant's regio and a Varushkan mandate of support.

Wasp nest.o: After the Highborn Assembly reaffirmed its peerless kinship with Navarr, Highborn priests went to Therunin to help lay its restless dead to rest. They found the worst-haunted region held by the Druj, and turned instead to new opportunities: a memorial glade, a cure for the poisoned Lower Tarn Valley, a Navarr wayhouse in Reikos and the defence of Peakedge Stead.

Watches from the Wall.o: Severin Teyhard von Holberg consecrated the gallery above Holberg's Holmauer Gate to Wisdom with true liao, backed without opposition by the Wisdom and League assemblies. A second, seemingly miraculous aura then settled on the gate itself, inspiring visionary dreams, spontaneous dedications to Wisdom and several new opportunities.

Watching my mistakes.o: With the Jotun driven out of Sermersuaq, Wintermark faced the legacy of their rule: resistance fighters who had made pacts with Blood-on-the-Snow, and monsters from the Winter and Summer realms loose in the wilds. The Empire was offered several ways to root out the Whisperer's allies during the Winter Solstice, and a proposal to build a hunting hall in the Suaq Wastes.

Watching you well.o: At the Assembly of Nine's request, the Silent Bell investigated the Hand of Dumon, a Suranni cult outlawed in the Empire, and reported on its nature, magic and aims, finding no link between the cult and the Black Plateau.

Watercolours in the rain.o: After Cold Sun's scions seized the Brilliant Star mithril mine in Tomari, its once-beneficial light became a permanent, dangerous bane that cuts production unless the Senate funds protection. The Pride Assembly's statements against Cold Sun also opened several proposed mandates to defend and celebrate Imperial art and culture.

Watered with fears.o: At the Winter Solstice Imperial magicians turned the Mournwold into a killing ground with combined Spring and Winter curses, slaughtering Jotun soldiers but also killing a sixth of the territory's civilians. The carnage provoked anger among Mournwold Marchers, unease among Wintermark's healers and fury among the Jotun.

Wayfaring strangers.o: Ahead of the Autumn 388YE summit, a series of foreign and Imperial visitors announced that they would come to Anvil seeking meetings. They included an Axou emissary, a mining guild threatening strikes in Tassato, the Karass, an Urizeni spire bearing a cursed Druj artefact, the crew of the Wraith King, Beoraidh gladiator maistirs and a feuding Tassatan merchant prince.

We all stand.o: In Autumn 386YE an Imperial Autumn enchantment over Mareave drew like-minded people together. Golden Pyramid magicians, Tamazi orcs, Marcher and Freeborn farmers, and League and Urizen builders pursued opportunities to develop the Empire's newest territory.

We are never ever getting back together.o: In the wake of the Rachensgrab raid, which shattered the international slave trade, this Wind of Fortune surveyed the Empire's foreign relations: the Liberty Pact's triumph, the hostility of Asavea and Jarm, an approach from the Grendel of Spiral, new Sarcophan trade offers, Suranni knights visiting Anvil and the Steward of Bregasland's terms for independence.

We are the storm.o: In Winter 387YE Emperor Vesna addressed the whole Empire. She celebrated the victory that had made the Sarangrave Imperial, urged citizens to settle former Druj lands, and called on them to fight the Jotun in Bregasland.

We give the future to the winds.o: Faraden's ambassador relayed a season of religious, military and trade news to the Empire. It included a covert priestly request for true liao to resist Asavean proselytising, confirmation that Faraden would keep its peace with the Jotun, and new trade openings in the Marches, Varushka and Dawn.

We've been here forever.o: After the Summer Solstice, six eternals answered the archmages' plenipotentiary messages and set out the terms, topics and times of their meetings at the Autumn Equinox. Eleonaris broke with custom by asking for a formal reception in the Imperial Senate.

Weak and idle theme.o: After the Iron Confederacy attacked and enslaved Suranni rebels sheltering in Feroz, the Zemress Islanders of Segura spread their outrage among the Freeborn, and conflicting Synod judgements left many questioning the Brass Coast's stance on slavery. The Wind offered a Synod mandate calling on Freeborn citizens to take up arms in defence of escaped slaves.

Weaving tangled nets.o: In Spring 388YE the Cold Sun incursion destroyed the small nation of Lantir and broke out of containment into Jarm, the Commonwealth and the neighbouring borderlands. Six Conclave orders and the Granite Pillar had offered aid to both rival powers, while diplomatic tensions over Imperial trade with Zemelslo continued.

Weight of the world.o: In Summer 383YE, Vasili Zoryakovich Zverokaz's Pride mandate prepared the people of newly conquered Ossium to accept the Way. Ser Ancél Watcher's questers found two more Druj miasma pillars. Locals still feared that the Druj would return, and the Empire faced a choice over the territory's many non-Druj orcs.

Weird Goodbye.o: In Winter 386YE the Cold Hand of Sarda icewalkers proposed tasks for the Icebarn twins, two Artok marked with runes after the Summer Solstice. Big Icebarn was sent to hunt the monsters of Agramant in Sermersuaq, and Little Icebarn was set to mine mithril at the Pride of Ikka's Tears.

Welly boots.o: In Summer 385YE four Imperial armies, the Tusks, the Strong Reeds, the Bounders and the Highborn Granite Pillar, moved to retake Bregasland, only to find that the Jotun and Mathilda Fisher had already fled. The liberation left lingering grudges, a looted Breadbasket and several open opportunities for the Marches.

What did the deep say?.o: Following the Autumn Equinox, five eternals (Barien, Ephisis, Janon, Siakha and Tharim) publicly answered the plenipotentiary messages sent by the Archmages, most accepting formal parley at the coming summit. Siakha's reply came by way of a monstrous shark-like beast and explicitly refused parley.

What regulates the wheel?.o: In the Winter of 387YE the Imperial regio at Anvil lost its power to empower rituals, the entrance to the Hall of Worlds moved away from it, and mysterious magnitude 30 shrouds settled over the Empire and its neighbouring territories. Meanwhile a celestial conjunction let covens of the same nation work together freely during the Winter Solstice.

What shall we do now?.o: In Spring 387YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Citadels of Axos, which were slowly warming but strained by trade risks, a vague Imperial reference to a pact, and the loss of Therunin. Imperial priests had also helped the Axou largely cleanse the haunted ruins of Solokha.

What will be, was not.o: Following three upheld Synod mandates from the Winter Solstice, Imperial citizens began withholding materials from the public auction at Anvil and looking for ways to strengthen their own nations. No white granite reached the auction, and several national ministries were proposed in response.

What's good for me.o: The Summer Solstice 384YE foreign affairs Wind of Fortune set out the Empire's dealings with neighbouring and distant nations. It covered the Liberty Pact, Sarcophan trade, a Jarmish ultimatum, the Thule alliance, Mathilda Fisher's demand for an independent Bregasland, Grendel activity in Spiral and Mareave, and a Suranni request to help crush the Hand of Dumon.

When I met you.o: Ahead of the Summer Solstice 387YE, a range of visitors sent word that they would come to Anvil seeking meetings. They included a merrow steading from Therunin, a dying Jotun jarl, Varushkan families and traders, and Freeborn showmen with a captured mandowla.

When Spring comes.o: In Autumn 385YE the Marches faced several crises. Siakha's shark-like heralds ravaged Mitwold until the Drakes drove them off, Bregasland seethed with accusations of collaboration with Mathilda Fisher, and the egregore Jack confirmed that the Mournwold Orcs could become Marchers.

When all the land is in ruins.o: In Winter 382YE the vallorn of Brocéliande surged against the liberated regions of Boar's Dell and Elerael. Some three thousand Navarr held it back for the season, while the Empire weighed reinforcements, Synod mandates, eternal aid and even abandoning the territory.

When all this was trees.o: In autumn 380YE the orcs of the Great Forest, formerly the Peytaht, left the Barrens and entered Therunin's Tarn Valley at the invitation of Therunin's Senator, Caerwyn Summercrow. They brought an army of around two thousand and most of their nation, after the Senate declared them foreigners rather than enemies at the Summer Solstice.

When peace was far away.o: In Winter 387YE the Civil Service reported on relations with the Principalities of Jarm, which remained at peace with the Empire but under embargo. Trade via the Jarmish protectorate of Zemelslo had opened, and Jarm made several offers, including a proposal to fortify and take full control of its embassy in Cargo.

When something is lost.o: In Autumn 388YE a potent Night enchantment settled over Madruga just as the Drakes and the Star Forged brought Siroc Bayou and Crucible into the Empire. The Star Forged emerged triumphant, but the six-thousand-strong Drakes vanished inside Crucible and now need rescuing.

When the ship comes in.o: In Summer 381YE, a Wind of Fortune reported that Imperial missionaries had spread the Doctrines of the Howling Abyss and the Ancestors to foreign followers of the Way. It also surveyed the Empire's relations and trade opportunities with Asavea, Axos, Jarm, Sumaah, Faraden, the Sarcophan Delves, the Commonwealth and the orc nations.

Where do we go from here?.o: Adamant's koboldi completed the Crucible of Fate in Zenith's Spire Calator, hastened by an Autumn ritual, giving the Urizen Assembly the chance to enact a mandate that would lift Zenith from being bereft of hope after the Druj desolation.

Where five winds meet.o: Faraden's ambassador answered Imperial approaches on trade, delegations and a possible trading enclave, while the Empire weighed its response to the Asavean attack on Meade, which had been launched from Faraden waters. The Senate abrogated the Gloaming Road during the summit.

Where the river rises.o: After Freeborn ritualists broke the banks of the Scorrero to cleanse the Blight from Madruga, the river flooded along its whole course, killing or injuring hundreds in Kahraman and Segura. In Madruga, the floodwaters transformed the southern Great Grasses and Siroc Plains into a strange, magic-infused marsh.

Where the slow river flows.o: In Spring 388YE the Empire's armies held eastern Mitwold against the Lasambrian Jotun and, led by the Wintermark Green Shield, drove them out of the Meadows after a horrific battle at Wayford. The Jotun still held Meade March, including the city of Meade, and Oddmire.

Whispering wind.o: In Winter 379YE a magical wind blew across the Brass Coast, whispering to the hakima a warning about the troubles facing the Coast and an invitation to a council at dusk on the first full day of the next summit at Anvil.

Whither the seed.o: After the Navarr's Wither the Seed curse on vallorn-held Brocéliande began to devastate the fertility of the Navarr living there, the Navarr Assembly urged the nation to find a way to lift it. Several possible routes emerged, each with its own heavy cost.

Who benefits?.o: In the run-up to the Spring Equinox 383YE, six eternals answered plenipotentiary messages from the Imperial archmages. Phaleron, Lashonar and Cathan Canae arranged meetings, Sorin sent a herald instead, and Ephisis and Arhallogen declined to parley.

Who can you trust?.o: After nearly ten thousand Imperial scouts joined the Karass in spying on the Thule and Druj in the Forest of Ulnak, the Empire gained an unexpected chance to seize a Druj black lotus plant at the Fetid Heart in Ghul'thak Forest. Doing so would certainly provoke a major diplomatic incident with the Thule.

Who counts the path untaken?.o: The Jotun swiftly retook the land the Empire had seized in Skallahn, and preparations moved forward for the hetjuveisla at Gull's Isle Hall and for a proposed Loyalty consecration of a shrine at the new Meeting Place.

Who goes there?.o: Several groups and individuals announced plans to come to Anvil for the Summer Solstice, each with business of their own. They included a Dawnish enchanter, a Highborn scholar, a Hahnmark coven, mountebanks, a Navarr steading, Wintermark mystics and a Summer herald seeking help.

Wide azure skies.o: In Spring 388YE the Grendel, reinforced by two navies and fresh armies sailing from Redoubt, drove the Seventh Wave and Winter Sun out of Fleisardh and pushed halfway into Clisearn. Magical citadels, an enchanted fortress and Skouran mercenaries slowed but could not halt them.

Wild blue yonder.o: In Summer 385YE the Empire's foreign relations were in flux: the Grendel were quietly furious over Spiral's defection, Asavean warships and privateers struck at Imperial and Liberty Pact interests, and relations with Faraden kept improving. A Grendel breakaway enclave also refused to accept Imperial rule in Spiral.

Wild is the wind.o: The Civil Service's Summer 387YE report on Faraden covered trade, diplomacy and religion. It noted Faraden disappointment at the Imperial withdrawal from Reinos, set out new opportunities for Faraden markets and caravanseri, and reported a Faraden war-wizard delegation and an assassination attempt by the Cinders.

Wildest dreams.o: Sarcombe in Southmoor grew in prosperity three years after receiving its charter, and the Marches were presented with several opportunities in the Mournwold: a canal to Meade, new civic offices, forest clearance, deeper mines and a green iron outpost. At the same time, Jotun threats linked to the traitor Stephen of Sarcombe were pressing on the territory.

Will to survive.o: After the Mournwold fell to the Jotun, friars from the isolated village of Whittle began openly preaching Hatred as the secret of their long survival, spreading hallowed weapons and consecrations among Marchers and Imperial soldiers. The Synod was offered a choice to support or denounce the spread of Hatred, and several armies gained a new order.

Will you believe?.o: Sumaah missionaries preached along the Empire's southern coast, denouncing the Imperial Synod and promoting Timoj over Bastion as the heart of the Way. At the Winter Solstice the Synod rejected several rival responses and backed Jorma Steelhail's mandate urging the Empire and Sumaah to seek common ground.

Willow and rain.o: In Summer 387YE the vallorn unleashed by the Druj in Therunin began to spread across the territory, with its miasma reaching into northern Morrow, while only Ossegrahn's protection kept Peakedge Stead alive. That protection would end unless his price was paid by the end of the Summer Solstice.

Windfall.o: After Salt Lord Kaliact's treaty let the Wolves of War take Spiral in a single season, the League egregores Harlequin and Innamorata weighed whether Kaliact's Apulian Orcs could join the League, setting a final decision for Saturday of the Summer Solstice summit. The Senate was left to settle the territory's name, its senator and the Legacy mithril mine.

Winds and flames.o: In Summer 386YE, Faraden relations with the Empire were broadly positive under the new Liege of the Five Winds, though some Faraden, led by High Lady Togene, resented the Marcher ambassador. Faraden sought a replacement for the destroyed Moonwater Hall and would welcome an Imperial move against Jotun-held Reinos.

Wise and measured.o: In Spring 388YE the new Axou ambassador, Ilarch Kario Skopos of Solokha, reported cordial relations with the Empire after Ambassador Hrafnar's "wise and measured words" eased tensions over the executed Scions of Cavan. Axos reaffirmed it would evict the orcs of Thornfen once the Senate confirms the treaty ceding the region.

Wish you were here.o: Ahead of the Spring Equinox 387YE, a variety of visitors sent word that they would come to Anvil, among them a Grendel envoy under a flag of parley, the Stzena of Tears with a plaguewulf, orcs from Beoraidh, a Kallavesi hermit and Great Forest Orcs keeping a promise to Wintermark.

With a flower, with a flame.o: A Spring 384YE Wind of Fortune reported new magical fortifications in Hahnmark, Bregasland and Kallavesa, shrouds shifting to the Brass Coast and a wondrous light show over Bastion. It also set out many eternal-led opportunities, including the contest for patronage of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun and a conjunction to rescue fleeing Suranni magicians.

Without a plea for mercy.o: In Winter 382YE the fading influence of Severin von Holberg's encyclical left several Synod matters in play: Winterfolk priests urged to turn their congregations into fighting units, a Freeborn call to free more slaves, the idolatrous works of the Asavean Architect, and a brewing doctrinal crisis over orc exemplars.

Wolf in summer.o: In Summer 379YE a ritual curse, Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence, fell on all four great League cities, halving the crystal mana produced in League territories and souring tempers during a sweltering heatwave until it faded after the Summer Solstice.

Words to make things right.o: In Autumn 382YE, the Woods-that-fell Feni, displaced by the great sinkhole, kept raiding for survival in Hahnmark and the Mournwold. Envoys arranged to come to Anvil to speak for them, and the Empire learned it could destroy both them and the Alderly Feni by force if it chose.

Workers in struggle.o: In Autumn 381YE, three opportunities arose around Imperial resources: an expedition into the Northern Sinkhole, a mithril heist at the Great Mine of Briante, and a marshwalker attack on the Feverwater dredgers. The sinkhole was named "Lorenzo's Deep Pockets", and the new Delver of the Depths funded the expedition.

Woven as a weapon.o: The Senate commissioned Graciana i Lopez i Guerra to appraise ways of making the trod network more effective at depleting the vallorn. She identified two costly options, a major wayhouse-building programme and a Synod mandate for a mass pilgrimage, plus an untested idea blocked by Aquillian Effugere's sorcery conviction.

Write the lines.o: After the Jotun withdrew from Sermersuaq, they left behind fortresses, a half-built smokehouse and an expanded mithril mine, and the Empire was offered several ways to use or remove them. The Thule also offered ilium for food and hunting rights, while a Jotun force advanced on the Fortress of Kalant.

Write your own ending.o: After the Empire drove the Druj out of Zenith and the territory was returned to Urizen, Imperial efforts turned to restoring a land left ruined, stifled by miasma and bereft of hope. The page set out the territory's condition and a range of opportunities to rebuild it.

Written in salt.o: Imperial Orc reavers answering Skywise Gralka's call found the freed orcs of Axos living in dreadful conditions, but the nation lacked the ships to help them. The page proposed a Synod mandate urging Imperial fleet captains to carry them to the Empire before the Commonwealth did so itself, and Gralka later enacted that mandate after the Winter Solstice.

Years of an inch and a step.o: In Winter 382YE the costs of the Highborn pilgrimage to walk the trods against the vallorn, shared across the Empire after every national assembly urged support for the grey pilgrims, were set to ease within a season. The Highborn Assembly then passed three mandates defining the pilgrims' religious mission.

You belong with me.o: Young Great Forest Orcs sheltering in Therunin asked the Navarr Assembly to endorse permanent settlements in Hercynia and Miaren, a step likely to lead to requests to join the Navarr nation. The Synod was offered a welcoming mandate, a stronger sworn welcome, or a cautionary mandate urging the orcs to move on.

You can't count on me.o: In Spring 385YE a round-up of magical incidents and opportunities was reported across the Empire. Highlights included a Summer enchantment over the Mournwold, the discovery that the Imperial Crown was still legally interdicted, and new magical fortifications and shrouds.

You could be happy.o: Following greater-majority Synod judgements urging vigilance against the Druj, the Dawnish, Navarr, Urizen and Varushkan Assemblies all enacted mandates sending citizens to patrol their borders with the Mallum. The Varushkan Assembly also had the chance to push the Iron Helms away from cruelty towards dark magic and curses, but the Eyes of Loyalty were turned on that mandate.

You do it to yourself.o: Following the Winter Solstice 385YE Synod's decisive rebuke of the cry "Death to the Druj", the Empire faced the open question of what to do about the Druj. The civil service set out two competing General Assembly mandates: commit utterly to victory over the Druj, or treat them as only one threat among many.

You know the night.o: Divisions over the brutal tactics of the Varushkan Iron Helms deepened in Winter 381YE, splitting the Empire's nations into rival camps and offering the Imperial Orc and Varushkan assemblies mandates to take sides. The Imperial Orcs declined to remake the Summer Storm, while Varushka chose to have all its soldiers embrace their heritage.

You'll recognise yourself.o: As the fame of Lorenzo 'la Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar and his cleaver-adorned works spread, his supporters proposed making him a sole Master of Commissions while detractors urged the Senate to hand the power of commission to the Imperial Synod. A slate of possible commissions emerged, some courting his patronage and others pointedly refusing it.

Your hand in mine.o: Naomi of Virtue's Rest, sent by Senate motion to appraise solutions to the Nesustak Forest rebels, failed to open talks but identified a single Sentinel Gate conjunction allowing five Imperial envoys to meet the rebels in Sarangrave.
